Yes. That was the clerk. Not fussy. Not old. Protected. He lived inside a system where inconvenience moved downhill and he had arranged to be uphill. I read the next line. Lyssa closed her eyes.</p><p>"Better."</p><p>I kept going. At the end of page twelve she sat up.</p><p>"Again?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>"No?"</p><p>"You know it enough to ruin it if you keep going."</p><p>I stared.</p><p>"That is what Teren said."</p><p>"I am smarter than Teren."</p><p>"You don't know Teren."</p><p>"I don't need to."</p><p>Fair. I put the pages down. The bag was packed. Mostly. There were still decisions available if I wanted them. Another shirt. More food. Different cord. A small knife. The drawing. I did not touch the drawer. Lyssa stood. For a moment I thought she was leaving. Instead she took my crutches and moved them away from the bed.</p><p>"What are you doing?"</p><p>"Making room."</p><p>"For what?"</p><p>She looked at me. Oh.</p><p>"That was a stupid question."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>She came back and stood between my knees. I put my hands on her hips. She touched the side of my face. Neither of us said anything useful. Then she kissed me. The first kiss was easy. The second was not. I pulled her closer. She shifted one knee onto the bed beside me, careful of my left side without looking at it, and kissed me until I stopped thinking about page twelve. That took less time than expected. I felt them anyway.</p><p>"It's five days."</p><p>"Maybe six."</p><p>"Six."</p><p>"Gregory."</p><p>"I'll come back."</p><p>She nodded. Then immediately reached past me and pulled the bag closer.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"You forgot socks."</p><p>I stared at her.</p><p>"I did not."</p><p>She opened the bag. I had forgotten socks.</p><p>"Fuck."</p><p>"I know."</p><p>I got up. Lyssa sat in the warm hollow I left on the mattress while I crossed to the drawer. The socks were in the second drawer. The drawing was in the first. I opened the second. Took three pairs. Closed it. Lyssa watched me.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Nothing."</p><p>I put the socks in the bag. She did not ask what was in the other drawer. Good. I tied the bag shut. Then untied it because the sweet cake was still on the table. Lyssa laughed.</p><p>"Shut up."</p><p>"I didn't say anything."</p><p>I packed the cake. Retied the bag. This time I left it closed. Tomorrow before sunrise I would get into a wagon with actors, scenery, bad wheels, too many scripts, and no reliable answer about where I would sleep. I was looking forward to it. That seemed unwise. I went back to Lyssa. There was still an evening left.</p></article>

waited.</p><p>Then moved.</p><p>Slow.</p><p>Painfully slow now because my hands had been gripping too hard from adrenaline and the floor was cluttered.</p><p>Outside air hit.</p><p>Cold.</p><p>Lyssa was there.</p><p>Not calmly.</p><p>She saw me.</p><p>Her whole body changed.</p><p>Then she crossed the distance fast.</p><p>“Where the fuck were you?”</p><p>“Behind you.”</p><p>“You were not behind me.”</p><p>“I was behind you. I was simply becoming increasingly behind you.”</p><p>She stared.</p><p>Bad time.</p><p>“Sorry.”</p><p>Better.</p><p>She grabbed my shirt.</p><p>Not the crutches.</p><p>Not my arm.</p><p>Shirt.</p><p>“I thought you were still inside.”</p><p>“I was.”</p><p>“That is the problem.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>She looked at my face.</p><p>“Are you hurt?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Burned?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Hand?”</p><p>“Fine.”</p><p>“Leg?”</p><p>“Fine.”</p><p>“Why do you have paper?”</p><p>I looked down.</p><p>Still holding the page.</p><p>“I was in the play.”</p><p>Lyssa blinked.</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>That was wrong.</p><p>“I was not in the play.”</p><p>She looked at the paper.</p><p>Then at the theatre.</p><p>Then at me.</p><p>“Greg.”</p><p>“I read one line.”</p><p>Her mouth opened.</p><p>Closed.</p><p>“You acted?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Did the audience hear you?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Did someone answer you?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That&#x27;s acting.”</p><p>“That is not a sufficient definition.”</p><p>She laughed.</p><p>Angry laugh.</p><p>Relieved laugh.</p><p>Then she hugged me.</p><p>Careful of crutches only because she had learned where they were.</p><p>I leaned into her.</p><p>For a while neither of us said anything.</p><p>Behind us the troupe was still working.</p><p>Buckets.</p><p>Doors.</p><p>Arguments.</p><p>Someone shouted about a missing wig.</p><p>The building had almost caught fire and someone cared about a wig.</p><p>I liked them immediately.</p><p>This was concerning.</p><p>Lyssa pulled back.</p><p>“Our date caught fire.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You said not intentionally dangerous.”</p><p>“You said that.”</p><p>“I did.”</p><p>“Your prediction failed.”</p><p>She shoved my shoulder.</p><p>“Asshole.”</p><p>We found food very late.</p><p>Not good food.</p><p>Everything good was closing.</p><p>We sat on a low wall again.</p><p>Apparently this was becoming ours.</p><p>Lyssa stole half my bread.</p><p>I told her about the painted tree.</p><p>The chair.</p><p>The bucket line.</p><p>The actor who became someone else the instant he stepped through the curtain.</p><p>The evacuation hidden inside a joke.</p><p>I did not tell her what I thought it meant.</p><p>I did not know.</p><p>At the end I showed her the page.</p><p>She read the marked line.</p><p>“No man who intends to return.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That got a laugh?”</p><p>“The second time.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“I don&#x27;t know.”</p><p>She smiled.</p><p>“That bothers you.”</p><p>“Deeply.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>We walked home.</p><p>At the lodging door she kissed me.</p><p>Long enough that I forgot the theatre for several seconds.</p><p>Useful.</p><p>Then she said:</p><p>“You liked the play.”</p><p>“Before the fire.”</p><p>“And during.”</p><p>“I did not like the fire.”</p><p>“You liked the weird people.”</p><p>I looked back toward the distant street.</p><p>Smoke was no longer visible.</p><p>“I do not know them.”</p><p>“Mm.”</p><p>“That is not an argument.”</p><p>“Goodnight, Greg.”</p><p>She left.</p><p>I went inside.</p><p>The keeper looked at the soot on my shirt.</p><p>“Date?”</p><p>I looked down.</p><p>Dark green.</p><p>Still dark green.</p><p>Mostly.</p><p>“Technically.”</p><p>She nodded as if this explained everything.</p><p>Upstairs, I found the folded play page still in my pocket.</p><p>I put it on the table.</p><p>Not the notebook.</p><p>The table.</p><p>Tomorrow no magic.</p><p>The day after, Hessa.</p><p>The theatre had not asked me to come back.</p><p>Good.</p><p>I was not going back.</p><p>Probably.<br/></p></article>
- `light/111.html:16`: <article class="prose light-prose"><p>My hands were mildly offended by yesterday.</p><p>Not injured.</p><p>Offended.</p><p>The distinction mattered because Hessa asked.</p><p>“Pain?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Numbness?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Weakness?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Thumb?”</p><p>“Normal.”</p><p>“Residual limb?”</p><p>“Baseline.”</p><p>“Calf?”</p><p>“Tired yesterday. Fine this morning.”</p><p>“Palms?”</p><p>I opened both hands.</p><p>“Warm yesterday. Fine now.”</p><p>Hessa inspected them anyway.</p><p>She pressed the right thumb pad.</p><p>Then the palm.</p><p>Then wrist.</p><p>Then forearm.</p><p>Nothing.</p><p>She checked the residual limb because she was Hessa and because apparently no part of me was allowed to become irrelevant merely because today's question concerned my arm.</p><p>“Pessa?”</p><p>“Stakes.”</p><p>Hessa looked up.</p><p>“That is not an activity.”</p><p>“It was when she did it.”</p><p>“What did you do?”</p><p>“Walked around them badly.”</p><p>“Fall?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Near fall?”</p><p>“Small hop once. No catch.”</p><p>“Hands?”</p><p>“Hot by the end.”</p><p>“Stopped?”</p><p>“She stopped me.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>I did not tell her that I had wanted another repetition after she stopped me.</p><p>It was not medically relevant.</p><p>Probably.</p><p>Hessa sat back.</p><p>“Today we draw.”</p><p>I tried not to look disappointed.</p><p>Failed.</p><p>She noticed.</p><p>“Do you want me to choose a test because your face is irritating?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>“Are we shaping?”</p><p>“I have not decided.”</p><p>That was worse.</p><p>She prepared the table.</p><p>Folded towel.</p><p>Copper.</p><p>Today the strip was straight again.</p><p>No charcoal on my hand.</p><p>No charcoal on my forearm.</p><p>I stared at the table.</p><p>Hessa said, “Leave the setup alone.”</p><p>“I am only looking.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“You cannot stop me thinking.”</p><p>“I did not ask you to stop thinking.”</p><p>Fair.</p><p>I sat.</p><p>Right forearm on towel.</p><p>Left hand loose.</p><p>Right foot planted.</p><p>Residual limb supported.</p><p>Crutches against the wall where I could see them.</p><p>“Minimal draw,” Hessa said.</p><p>“Nothing else?”</p><p>“Nothing else.”</p><p>I drew.</p><p>Familiar now.</p><p>Not easy.</p><p>Familiar.</p><p>Mana gathered through the routes I knew without becoming ordinary.</p><p>Trunk.</p><p>Arms.</p><p>Right side.</p><p>Left thigh to knee.</p><p>Nothing unusual below it.</p><p>Ordinary phantom left foot somewhere under the table, heel angled slightly inward.</p><p>Not magical.</p><p>Probably not even worth noting unless asked.</p><p>“Stable,” Hessa said.</p><p>I held.</p><p>Copper responded.</p><p>No thumb sensation.</p><p>No wrist movement.</p><p>No shaping.</p><p>“Release.”</p><p>I released.</p><p>Hessa waited.</p><p>I waited.</p><p>She checked pulse.</p><p>Hand.</p><p>Thumb.</p><p>Grip.</p><p>“Fine?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>She wrote.</p><p>I watched.</p><p>“You said draw.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You did not say draw only.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“So now?”</p><p>“Now I know you can come in the day after Pessa makes your hands hot, perform a minimal draw, and not immediately produce a hand symptom.”</p><p>“That seems unsurprising.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>I hated when boring pleased her.</p><p>She looked at me.</p><p>“Do you know why I care?”</p><p>“Because the previous thumb symptom happened in a hand that also bears crutch load, and yesterday was the first substantial movement session since before the shaping tests.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>“So this is not a shaping test.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Are we done?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>I leaned back.</p><p>Hessa kept writing.</p><p>I did not ask again.</p><p>This lasted approximately nine seconds.</p><p>“What would make it not done?”</p><p>She sighed.</p><p>“Your inability to tolerate silence.”</p><p>“That is not medical.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She set the pen down.</p><p>“Tell me what you think happened when I said stop last time.”</p><p>I had thought about this.</p><p>Not practiced.</p><p>Thought.</p><p>Allowed.</p><p>“I reduced the forward change.”</p><p>“Know or think?”</p><p>“Think.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Subjectively it stopped moving toward the line.”</p><p>“And then?”</p><p>“It widened.”</p><p>“Did you choose widening?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Did you choose not to widen?”</p><p>I paused.</p><p>“That sounds like the same question.”</p><p>“It isn't.”</p><p>I replayed the sensation.</p><p>The stop cue.</p><p>The effort to stop.</p><p>The broadening.</p><p>“I was trying to stop changing it.”</p><p>“Everything about it?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Were you trying to hold the shape you had?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Were you trying to return it to the original draw?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Were you trying to release?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She nodded.</p><p>“What did your body do?”</p><p>“No wrist rotation.”</p><p>“I know what I saw.”</p><p>Right.</p><p>My report.</p><p>“Forearm felt tense.”</p><p>“Muscular?”</p><p>“Maybe. Not strongly.”</p><p>“Hand?”</p><p>“Quiet.”</p><p>“Breathing?”</p><p>I frowned.</p><p>“I don't know.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>She wrote that.</p><p>“You are delighted by ignorance.”</p><p>“I am delighted when you stop replacing it.”</p><p>She picked up a charcoal stick.</p><p>My attention sharpened.</p><p>Hessa saw that too.</p><p>“Do not celebrate.”</p><p>“I am not.”</p><p>“You are nineteen. Your entire face is celebrating.”</p><p>She drew one short line on the inside of my right forearm.</p><p>Farther from the wrist than last time.</p><p>Then another line closer to the elbow.</p><p>Two again.</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>“One attempt?”</p><p>“If we do it.”</p><p>“If?”</p><p>“I can still decide not to.”</p><p>I shut up.</p><p>Miracle.</p><p>Hessa placed the copper.</p><p>“Different question,” she said.</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>“That was not praise.”</p><p>“What question?”</p><p>“Last time I told you to stop altering while holding the draw.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You interpreted that as freeze the alteration.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Today, if we proceed, I may ask something narrower.”</p><p>I waited.</p><p>She pointed to the nearer charcoal line.</p><p>“You will draw. I will tell you whether to alter toward the near or far mark. You will begin one small alteration. Then I will say enough.”</p><p>“Instead of stop.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“What does enough mean?”</p><p>“End the deliberate alteration and allow the mana to settle back toward the underlying draw without releasing the draw.”</p><p>I stared.</p><p>“That is harder.”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>“It is also different.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Last time I was trying to hold the altered state.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Now you want me to stop maintaining it.”</p><p>“I want to know whether you can stop feeding the deliberate change without dropping everything.”</p><p>That was cleaner.</p><p>Also terrifying.</p><p>“External effect?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Barrier?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Left?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Second attempt if I fail?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>Of course.</p><p>“What counts as failure?”</p><p>“I will tell you afterward.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“You know.”</p><p>“I know some things I would stop for. I do not know every way you can fail before you do it.”</p><p>Fair.</p><p>I hated fair.</p><p>She examined my right hand one more time.</p><p>“Any tingling now?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Pain?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Numbness?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Cold?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Ready?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Minimal draw.”</p><p>I drew again.</p><p>The second draw of the day felt slightly less crisp.</p><p>Not weaker.</p><p>More aware.</p><p>That could have been attention.</p><p>I said nothing.</p><p>“Stable?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>Hessa watched.</p><p>Copper answered.</p><p>“Far mark.”</p><p>I began.</p><p>Small.</p><p>Not thumb.</p><p>Not hand.</p><p>Forearm.</p><p>The alteration gathered as a narrow pressure of awareness, not physical pressure, moving along the inside of the right forearm.</p><p>Not a line exactly.</p><p>More like a region with a direction.</p><p>It approached the far mark.</p><p>“Enough.”</p><p>I stopped feeding it.</p><p>That was the instruction.</p><p>Not freeze.</p><p>Not reverse.</p><p>Not release.</p><p>Stop feeding.</p><p>For half a second nothing happened.</p><p>Then the altered region softened.</p><p>Not disappeared.</p><p>Softened.</p><p>The edge nearest my wrist faded first.</p><p>The center remained.</p><p>Then the whole thing seemed to collapse inward.</p><p>My wrist twitched.</p><p>Tiny.</p><p>I felt it.</p><p>Hessa saw it.</p><p>“Release.”</p><p>I released immediately.</p><p>Mana gone.</p><p>The forearm sensation vanished with it.</p><p>My heart was beating harder than the test deserved.</p><p>Hessa touched my wrist.</p><p>“Pain?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Tingling?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Numbness?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Weak?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Cold?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Barrier?”</p><p>I thought.</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Anything familiar?”</p><p>“The wrist twitch.”</p><p>“Familiar how?”</p><p>“Movement. Not the setup.”</p><p>“Do not improve the answer.”</p><p>“I am not.”</p><p>She checked grip.</p><p>Fingertips.</p><p>Thumb.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Then she sat.</p><p>I waited.</p><p>She wrote.</p><p>I waited longer.</p><p>This was abuse.</p><p>Finally:</p><p>“You stopped feeding the alteration.”</p><p>I almost smiled.</p><p>She raised a finger.</p><p>“And then the pattern changed.”</p><p>Smile gone.</p><p>“How?”</p><p>“I saw the response diminish rather than broaden. Copper response reduced with it. Then your wrist moved.”</p><p>“Did I succeed?”</p><p>“You performed the instruction more closely than last time.”</p><p>“That is not yes.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Is it no?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>I stared.</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“You want a category before I have one.”</p><p>“I stopped shaping.”</p><p>“You stopped deliberately feeding the change. I am reasonably confident of that.”</p><p>That landed.</p><p>“Reasonably?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And it settled?”</p><p>“It changed toward less altered. That is what I observed.”</p><p>“Without dropping the draw.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>There.</p><p>Something in my chest lifted.</p><p>Hessa continued before I could turn it into a parade.</p><p>“You also had an involuntary or at least unrequested wrist movement at the end.”</p><p>“Tiny.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No Barrier pattern.”</p><p>“Not one I recognized.”</p><p>“So.”</p><p>“So I have one attempt where the alteration broadened after a stop instruction and one attempt where a differently framed instruction produced diminishing alteration followed by a wrist twitch.”</p><p>“That is better.”</p><p>“It is different.”</p><p>“It can be both.”</p><p>Hessa looked annoyed that I had said something reasonable.</p><p>I enjoyed this.</p><p>“Does this change external effect?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Casting?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Next test?”</p><p>“I don't know.”</p><p>My joy survived anyway.</p><p>That annoyed her more.</p><p>“You are not cleared to practice this.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“You are not cleared to draw.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“You are not cleared to shape.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“You are not cleared to reproduce the wrist movement.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Tomorrow no magic.”</p><p>I groaned.</p><p>“One day?”</p><p>“One day.”</p><p>“Then?”</p><p>“Come back the day after tomorrow.”</p><p>“Are we doing this again?”</p><p>“I don't know.”</p><p>Of course.</p><p>I stood.</p><p>No tingling.</p><p>Hand normal.</p><p>Palms normal.</p><p>Residual limb quiet.</p><p>I took the crutches.</p><p>Hessa said, “Greg.”</p><p>I stopped.</p><p>“You trained yesterday.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You tested today.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Tomorrow does not need to contain Pessa because it cannot contain me.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>She watched me.</p><p>I thought about lying.</p><p>Did not.</p><p>“I might ask Lyssa to do something.”</p><p>Hessa blinked.</p><p>“That sounds medically preferable.”</p><p>“Rude.”</p><p>“Go.”</p><p>I went.</p><p>Outside, Carrow was offensively normal.</p><p>Carts.</p><p>Bread.</p><p>Mud.</p><p>Someone shouting about lamp oil.</p><p>A dog asleep under a bench.</p><p>I had shaped mana.</p><p>I had maybe stopped shaping mana.</p><p>Reasonably.</p><p>Under a different instruction.</p><p>Once.</p><p>In a small supervised test.</p><p>Without a spell.</p><p>I wanted to tell everyone.</p><p>Instead I went to find Lyssa.</p><p>She was working.</p><p>So I waited.<br/></p></article>

- `light/122.html:16`: <article class="prose light-prose"><p>Hessa had covered the tray.</p><p>That was new.</p><p>Not dramatic.</p><p>A square of gray cloth over the part where the copper usually sat.</p><p>I noticed before I sat down.</p><p>She noticed me noticing.</p><p>“Hands first.”</p><p>“That is not copper.”</p><p>“Hands.”</p><p>Right thumb.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Fingers.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Wrist.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Forearm.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>She pressed along the inside of the arm, then checked grip, fingertips, wrist movement.</p><p>“Yesterday?”</p><p>“Theatre.”</p><p>“Magic?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Symptoms?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Training?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Fall?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Near fall?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Residual limb?”</p><p>“Baseline.”</p><p>“Phantom?”</p><p>“Ordinary.”</p><p>“Anything unusual below the left knee?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Hand urge?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Thumb?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She wrote.</p><p>I looked at the cloth.</p><p>She did not.</p><p>This was deliberate cruelty.</p><p>“Do you want to know what is under it?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>I waited.</p><p>She wrote another line.</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You are enjoying this.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“You are lying.”</p><p>“Possibly.”</p><p>She closed the notebook.</p><p>Then removed the cloth.</p><p>Copper.</p><p>Of course.</p><p>Also a narrow glazed tile.</p><p>A small upright wooden frame.</p><p>And from the top of the frame hung a single dark thread.</p><p>The thread ended above the tile.</p><p>Nothing touched it.</p><p>I stared.</p><p>Hessa watched my face.</p><p>“That is external.”</p><p>“It is a thread.”</p><p>“It is outside my body.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>She looked at me.</p><p>“Is this clearance?”</p><p>“For one question.”</p><p>I stopped breathing for a moment.</p><p>Not intentionally.</p><p>Hessa&#x27;s expression sharpened.</p><p>“Breathe.”</p><p>I did.</p><p>“One question,” she repeated. “One attempt. Under my instruction. This is not casting clearance. It is not Barrier clearance. It is not independent external work. It is not permission to reproduce the test.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Say the rest.”</p><p>“Left shaping remains excluded.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No independent draw.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No independent shaping.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No independent external attempt.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No spell.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>I looked at the thread again.</p><p>It was extremely unimpressive.</p><p>Perfect.</p><p>“What is the question?”</p><p>“Whether you can deliberately extend a small altered response beyond the boundary of the right forearm without releasing the underlying draw.”</p><p>I looked back at her.</p><p>“Extend.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Not release.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>“Not push.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>“Not cast.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>“Not Barrier.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>“How far?”</p><p>She pointed.</p><p>The thread hung less than a finger-width from where my right forearm would rest beside the frame.</p><p>“That far.”</p><p>“That is not a measurement.”</p><p>“It is enough of one.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“I measured before you arrived.”</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>She smiled.</p><p>Cruel woman.</p><p>“How far?”</p><p>“Three quarters of an inch from skin to thread when your arm is in position.”</p><p>Better.</p><p>“Why thread?”</p><p>“Light. Visible. Harmless. If it moves, we can see direction. If it does not move, we have a clean absence to discuss.”</p><p>“Air.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Breathing.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Table vibration.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Crutch movement.”</p><p>“You will be seated.”</p><p>“Door.”</p><p>“Closed.”</p><p>“Window.”</p><p>“Closed.”</p><p>“Your sleeve.”</p><p>“Rolled above the elbow.”</p><p>“My hand.”</p><p>“Still.”</p><p>“Your hand.”</p><p>“Not near it.”</p><p>“Copper response.”</p><p>“Separate observation.”</p><p>I stared at the apparatus.</p><p>“You thought about this.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>That should not have been surprising.</p><p>It was.</p><p>I had spent weeks wanting an external test.</p><p>Hessa had apparently spent at least some portion of that time deciding what one would need to mean.</p><p>The thread did not look like magic.</p><p>It looked like sewing.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Probably.</p><p>“What counts?”</p><p>Hessa pointed at the tile beneath it.</p><p>“There is a charcoal line directly below the thread&#x27;s resting position.”</p><p>I leaned closer.</p><p>There was.</p><p>“If the thread moves visibly away from rest while you are holding the requested state, I record direction and duration.”</p><p>“How much movement?”</p><p>“Visible.”</p><p>“That is subjective.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Can we mark distance?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Because your first external question is whether there is any reproducible-looking change worth measuring more precisely later.”</p><p>“Reproducible-looking is dangerous language.”</p><p>“It is.”</p><p>“Because one attempt cannot establish reproducibility.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>I liked her less when she agreed quickly.</p><p>“And if it moves once?”</p><p>“We record that it moved once.”</p><p>“External effect?”</p><p>“We record an observed external movement during the attempt.”</p><p>“That is cowardly.”</p><p>“That is accurate.”</p><p>“And if it does not move?”</p><p>“We record no observed external movement.”</p><p>“Failure.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“It is literally failure to move the thread.”</p><p>“It is failure to move the thread if moving the thread is the goal.”</p><p>“It is.”</p><p>“The goal is to learn whether your current control can produce an observable external change under this instruction.”</p><p>“That is moving the thread with extra words.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>I knew this argument.</p><p>I was going to lose it.</p><p>“What stops the test?”</p><p>“Any thumb tingling. Any urge to curl or spread fingers. Wrist movement. Weakness. Cold. Numbness. Pain. Familiar broad pattern. Any left-side change that is not ordinary phantom sensation. Any sense that you are trying to complete Barrier. Any urge to release forcefully. Any change you cannot describe well enough for me to decide whether to continue.”</p><p>“That last one is hostile.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“One attempt.”</p><p>“One.”</p><p>“If nothing happens, no second attempt?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“If I know what I did wrong?”</p><p>“Especially no.”</p><p>I sat.</p><p>She positioned my right forearm on a folded cloth beside the frame.</p><p>Not touching.</p><p>The thread hung near the inside of the forearm.</p><p>Three quarters of an inch suddenly looked enormous.</p><p>I could bridge it with a fingertip.</p><p>Not allowed.</p><p>My hand rested open on the table beyond my forearm.</p><p>Hessa adjusted the copper on the other side.</p><p>“Before draw.”</p><p>The thread was still.</p><p>Mostly.</p><p>Nothing in a room was perfectly still.</p><p>Tiny tremor.</p><p>Maybe air.</p><p>Maybe vision.</p><p>The charcoal line gave me a reference.</p><p>“Breathe normally,” Hessa said.</p><p>“That will move it.”</p><p>“Then we observe baseline first.”</p><p>We did.</p><p>I breathed.</p><p>The thread moved almost imperceptibly once.</p><p>Toward me.</p><p>Then back.</p><p>“Baseline movement,” Hessa said.</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Again.”</p><p>I breathed.</p><p>Nothing obvious.</p><p>Again.</p><p>Tiny movement.</p><p>Different direction.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Annoying.</p><p>“Do not hold your breath during the attempt.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“I am telling you anyway.”</p><p>She waited.</p><p>Then:</p><p>“Minimal draw.”</p><p>I drew.</p><p>Small.</p><p>Familiar enough to recognize.</p><p>Not easy.</p><p>Not automatic.</p><p>Copper responded.</p><p>Right forearm.</p><p>Ordinary phantom left foot.</p><p>No unusual extension.</p><p>No thumb.</p><p>No fingers.</p><p>“Hold.”</p><p>I held.</p><p>The thread remained thread.</p><p>“Small alteration. Right forearm. Toward the charcoal mark on your skin.”</p><p>There was a small mark near the wrist-side area again.</p><p>I shaped.</p><p>Localized.</p><p>Not perfect.</p><p>Small.</p><p>Copper changed.</p><p>“Report.”</p><p>“Alteration present. Small. Slightly broader toward elbow than the mark, but not shifting.”</p><p>“Motor?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Thumb?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Left?”</p><p>“Ordinary.”</p><p>“Good. Hold.”</p><p>I held.</p><p>The thread did nothing.</p><p>This was not yet the external instruction.</p><p>My heart had accelerated anyway.</p><p>That was inconvenient.</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Heart rate.”</p><p>“I can see.”</p><p>“Does that matter?”</p><p>“It may matter to you. Not enough to stop.”</p><p>Fine.</p><p>She watched my hand.</p><p>Then the copper.</p><p>Then the thread.</p><p>“Now listen carefully.”</p><p>I did.</p><p>“Do not release.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Do not increase the internal alteration.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Do not try to move your hand, wrist, or fingers.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Keep the underlying draw active.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“From the existing altered region only, attempt the smallest extension you can toward the thread.”</p><p>I stared at the thread.</p><p>“Extension.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Across the gap.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Stop if it feels like force.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Stop if it becomes broad.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Stop if I say stop.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>She waited.</p><p>“Reach.”</p><p>I tried.</p><p>Nothing happened.</p><p>Not to the thread.</p><p>Internally, the alteration changed.</p><p>I felt it narrow.</p><p>No.</p><p>Not narrow.</p><p>Lengthen?</p><p>Dangerous word.</p><p>The edge nearest the thread became more distinct.</p><p>I did not feel anything outside the skin.</p><p>I did not know what outside should feel like.</p><p>The thread remained still.</p><p>“Report,” Hessa said.</p><p>“Near edge sharper. Maybe narrower behind it.”</p><p>“External sensation?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Motor?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Continue only the same instruction. Do not increase force.”</p><p>I tried again.</p><p>Small.</p><p>The internal altered region seemed to lean toward the gap.</p><p>That was metaphor.</p><p>No.</p><p>It changed asymmetrically toward the thread.</p><p>Better.</p><p>Copper response changed.</p><p>The thread moved.</p><p>Tiny.</p><p>Toward my arm.</p><p>I froze.</p><p>Wrong.</p><p>Not release.</p><p>Not stop draw.</p><p>Hessa said, “Hold.”</p><p>I held.</p><p>The thread returned toward the charcoal line.</p><p>My heart was loud.</p><p>“Did you breathe differently?”</p><p>“I don&#x27;t know.”</p><p>“Good answer. Hold.”</p><p>The alteration remained.</p><p>No motor.</p><p>No thumb.</p><p>No cold.</p><p>“Again. Same extension. No more.”</p><p>I tried.</p><p>The thread did not move.</p><p>Nothing.</p><p>I wanted to try harder.</p><p>Did not.</p><p>“Report.”</p><p>“Internal asymmetry toward thread. No external sensation. No movement I can see.”</p><p>“I saw none.”</p><p>“First movement?”</p><p>“I saw it.”</p><p>“Cause?”</p><p>“Unknown.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>I hated that.</p><p>“Continue.”</p><p>“One attempt.”</p><p>“This is the same attempt.”</p><p>Fair.</p><p>I maintained draw.</p><p>Maintained alteration.</p><p>Tried the same smallest extension.</p><p>The thread moved again.</p><p>Not much.</p><p>This time sideways.</p><p>Not toward me.</p><p>To my left.</p><p>Then stopped.</p><p>Hessa immediately said:</p><p>“RETURN.”</p><p>External question over.</p><p>I obeyed.</p><p>Not release.</p><p>Reduce alteration.</p><p>The thread settled.</p><p>I did not watch it.</p><p>Right forearm.</p><p>RETURN.</p><p>The altered region diminished.</p><p>Wrist-side edge softened.</p><p>Center dimmed.</p><p>No motor urge.</p><p>No elbowward shift I could detect.</p><p>“Report.”</p><p>“Reducing. No motor. No thumb.”</p><p>“Continue.”</p><p>I did.</p><p>The alteration became uncertain.</p><p>“I cannot tell if residual remains.”</p><p>“Underlying draw?”</p><p>“Still present. Higher confidence.”</p><p>“Hold.”</p><p>I held.</p><p>Hessa watched copper.</p><p>Then my hand.</p><p>Then thread.</p><p>“Release.”</p><p>I released.</p><p>She took my right hand immediately.</p><p>Open.</p><p>Close.</p><p>Thumb.</p><p>Fingers.</p><p>Wrist.</p><p>Grip.</p><p>No symptom.</p><p>“Cold?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Numb?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Pain?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Urge?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Left?”</p><p>“Ordinary phantom.”</p><p>“Anything external now?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She waited.</p><p>I waited.</p><p>The thread hung above its charcoal line.</p><p>I wanted to accuse it of something.</p><p>Hessa wrote.</p><p>I could not read upside down from this angle.</p><p>Probably intentional.</p><p>“Well?”</p><p>“Sit.”</p><p>“I am sitting.”</p><p>“Then continue.”</p><p>Hostile.</p><p>She wrote longer than usual.</p><p>“What did you see?”</p><p>“I will tell you.”</p><p>“When?”</p><p>“When I am done writing what I saw before hearing what you want me to have seen.”</p><p>That was fair.</p><p>Horrible.</p><p>I looked at the thread.</p><p>First movement toward my arm.</p><p>Could be breath.</p><p>Second sideways.</p><p>Could be air.</p><p>Could be table.</p><p>Could be nothing.</p><p>Could be magic.</p><p>The last possibility was too large.</p><p>I tried to make it smaller.</p><p>Observed movement.</p><p>Unknown cause.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Hessa put the pencil down.</p><p>“Your report first.”</p><p>I gave it exactly.</p><p>Minimal draw.</p><p>Small alteration.</p><p>Near edge became more distinct after REACH.</p><p>Internal response became asymmetric toward thread.</p><p>No external sensation.</p><p>First visible thread movement toward arm.</p><p>I did not know whether breathing changed.</p><p>Second extension produced no observed movement.</p><p>Third produced a small sideways movement.</p><p>Then RETURN.</p><p>Alteration reduced.</p><p>No unwanted motor response.</p><p>No thumb.</p><p>No unusual left phantom.</p><p>Release normal.</p><p>Hessa nodded.</p><p>“My observation is close.”</p><p>“Close how?”</p><p>“Copper changed when you attempted extension.”</p><p>“That is expected.”</p><p>“Not necessarily.”</p><p>“Fine.”</p><p>“The internal altered response appeared to change directionally.”</p><p>“You can see that?”</p><p>“I can see enough through copper response to say it changed. Direction is partly your report.”</p><p>Important.</p><p>“The thread moved twice during the extension portion.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Once toward you. Once sideways.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“It also showed small baseline movement before draw.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“So?”</p><p>“So I cannot attribute either movement to you.”</p><p>Disappointment arrived cleanly.</p><p>Not devastating.</p><p>Just there.</p><p>“Then no external effect.”</p><p>“No established external effect.”</p><p>“That is different wording.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Did the test fail?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“What did it establish?”</p><p>“That I can ask you to attempt a bounded extension without you immediately releasing, broadening into the familiar pattern, recruiting your hand, or losing the underlying draw.”</p><p>I stopped.</p><p>She continued.</p><p>“And when I ended the external question, you returned the alteration without the previous unwanted responses.”</p><p>“That is internal control.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“So we learned internal control during an external test.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And the external result is unknown.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>I looked at the thread.</p><p>“You planned this.”</p><p>“I hoped for interpretable information.”</p><p>“You got the wrong information.”</p><p>“I got information.”</p><p>“Practitioner.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>I leaned back.</p><p>“Am I cleared for external testing now?”</p><p>“You were cleared for this external test.”</p><p>“That is not what I asked.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Can we repeat it?”</p><p>“Not today.”</p><p>“Tomorrow?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Day after?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>“How many living days?”</p><p>“Two.”</p><p>I stared.</p><p>“Again?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Because this was your first supervised attempt to deliberately extend an altered response beyond your body.”</p><p>“And nothing happened.”</p><p>“Unknown.”</p><p>“That is worse.”</p><p>“No. It is less satisfying.”</p><p>Same thing.</p><p>Not same thing.</p><p>Fine.</p><p>“Two full no-magic days?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then assessment?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Could the next assessment repeat the thread?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Could it use something else?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Could it return to internal control?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Could you decide external testing was premature?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You are impossible.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>I looked at the apparatus.</p><p>“Can I ask whether the sideways movement is more interesting than the movement toward me?”</p><p>“You can ask.”</p><p>“Is it?”</p><p>“Not enough to matter.”</p><p>“Because breath would more likely move it away?”</p><p>“Do not build airflow theory from your chair.”</p><p>“I know airflow.”</p><p>“You do not know this room&#x27;s airflow well enough.”</p><p>“Window closed.”</p><p>“Door closed.”</p><p>“Still convection.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Body heat.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Your movement.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Table vibration.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Thread twist.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Static?”</p><p>She paused.</p><p>“Possibly.”</p><p>I hated the universe.</p><p>“So the thread can move for six reasons.”</p><p>“More.”</p><p>“And magic is one candidate.”</p><p>“Possibly.”</p><p>“Possibly possibly.”</p><p>“That is where we are.”</p><p>I wanted a clean event.</p><p>A spark.</p><p>A twitch that happened exactly when I reached and nowhere else.</p><p>A thread leaping sideways three times in identical direction.</p><p>Something I could own.</p><p>Instead I had two tiny movements and a woman professionally refusing to let me have them.</p><p>Good.</p><p>No.</p><p>Accurate.</p><p>Probably good later.</p><p>Still irritating now.</p><p>Hessa uncovered the charcoal reference under the thread and checked where it rested.</p><p>“Back at baseline?”</p><p>“Approximately.”</p><p>“Approximately?”</p><p>“Thread has twist.”</p><p>I laughed.</p><p>She looked at me.</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“Nothing.”</p><p>“Gregory.”</p><p>“The first external magical test of my life may have been defeated by sewing.”</p><p>“It was not defeated.”</p><p>“Thread twist.”</p><p>“Is real.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“That is why we test small things.”</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>“Because small things reveal all the ways measurement is annoying.”</p><p>“Among other reasons.”</p><p>She removed the frame.</p><p>That felt abrupt.</p><p>The external world disappeared from the tray.</p><p>Copper remained.</p><p>I watched her put the thread apparatus on a shelf.</p><p>“Can I touch it?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“I meant later.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Because you will inspect the thread.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And the frame.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And the tile.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And then attempt to determine airflow.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And then arrive next time with a theory.”</p><p>I considered lying.</p><p>Did not.</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>Fair.</p><p>She made me sit another ten minutes.</p><p>Ordinary hand movement only.</p><p>No ritual.</p><p>She caught me checking the thumb once.</p><p>“Did it feel wrong?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Then stop.”</p><p>I drank water.</p><p>Reached for the cup.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Grip.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Crutches.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Three ordinary steps.</p><p>No tingling.</p><p>No finger urge.</p><p>No wrist movement.</p><p>No strange left phantom.</p><p>Hessa watched.</p><p>“Two days.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No magic.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Living.”</p><p>“Poorly specified.”</p><p>“Consistently effective.”</p><p>“That is not established.”</p><p>She pointed at the door.</p><p>I left.</p><p>Outside, Carrow had not changed.</p><p>This was offensive.</p><p>I had just attempted to affect something outside my body with mana.</p><p>Maybe.</p><p>Technically I had attempted.</p><p>The something had moved.</p><p>Maybe because of me.</p><p>Maybe because rooms contained air.</p><p>A cart passed.</p><p>Someone shouted about fish.</p><p>Two children were arguing over a hoop.</p><p>I stood near Hessa&#x27;s doorway and tried to decide what I felt.</p><p>Pleased.</p><p>Annoyed.</p><p>Hungry.</p><p>That seemed manageable.</p><p>Theatre was west.</p><p>Guild another direction.</p><p>Lyssa would be working or not.</p><p>Pessa had her own day.</p><p>Tomorrow had no magic.</p><p>The day after also had no magic.</p><p>Then Hessa.</p><p>I could spend forty-eight hours thinking about thread.</p><p>Absolutely not.</p><p>I started walking.</p><p>West.</p><p>Then stopped.</p><p>Not because theatre was wrong.</p><p>Because I was hungry and the food stall I wanted was east.</p><p>I turned east.</p><p>This was not symbolic.</p><p>It was lunch.</p><p>Probably.</p></article>

pace.</p><p>Two crutches.</p><p>Right foot.</p><p>Turn.</p><p>Not Pessa's turn.</p><p>Just a turn.</p><p>I did not analyze it.</p><p>Mostly.</p><p>“Again.”</p><p>I went.</p><p>Back.</p><p>No Ground floor. Sitting. Maybe an hour.”</p><p>Perfect.</p><p>Exactly the kind of thing I could do.</p><p>I looked toward the side room.</p><p>Then at the meat roll.</p><p>Then back at Merrin.</p><p>“No.”</p><p>He blinked once.</p><p>“All right.”</p><p>That was it.</p><p>No inquiry into my recovery.</p><p>No disappointment.</p><p>He turned to the next person.</p><p>I stood there holding food.</p><p>This had happened before.</p><p>Still weird.</p><p>Jorren was not there.</p><p>Alden was not there.</p><p>Pessa was somewhere beyond the yard, maybe.</p><p>No one required me.</p><p>I finished the meat roll.</p><p>Then I went upstairs.</p><p>Not lodging upstairs.</p><p>Guild upstairs.</p><p>Stopped.</p><p>No.</p><p>That was stupid.</p><p>I did not need to climb stairs to prove I could make an unproductive choice.</p><p>I turned around.</p><p>Ugly turn.</p><p>Worked.</p><p>Outside again.</p><p>A boy was floating folded paper boats down the gutter left by the rain.</p><p>Not a child I knew.</p><p>One boat caught under a cart rut.</p><p>He poked it with a stick.</p><p>Missed.</p><p>Poked again.</p><p>Freed it.</p><p>The boat spun once and continued.</p><p>I watched until it vanished under a bridge stone.</p><p>Then I walked home.</p><p>The keeper was repairing a loose hinge on the pantry door.</p><p>She had the pin out and was tapping it straight against the floor with a small hammer.</p><p>“Need help?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>Good.</p><p>I sat at the bottom table.</p><p>She hammered.</p><p>I watched.</p><p>After a while she said, “You have somewhere to be?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She nodded.</p><p>Hammer.</p><p>Turn pin.</p><p>Hammer.</p><p>Check.</p><p>“Could be better.”</p><p>“Probably.”</p><p>“Door still opens.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>She put the pin back.</p><p>The hinge remained quiet.</p><p>I did not write it down immediately.</p><p>That was perhaps the most impressive thing I did all day.</p><p>Eventually, I went upstairs.</p><p>Fourteen steps.</p><p>Slow.</p><p>Rail.</p><p>Crutches.</p><p>Right leg.</p><p>Pause at the landing.</p><p>No drama.</p><p>In my room, the repaired tavern chair sat by the window.</p><p>I sat.</p><p>Carrow outside.</p><p>Wet roofs.</p><p>People moving.</p><p>Someone shouted about onions in the distance.</p><p>Possibly the same seller.</p><p>Probably not.</p><p>The world contained many onion problems.</p><p>I opened the notebook.</p><p>Wrote:</p><p>Minimal supervised draw. No shaping. No immediate thumb tingling during draw or brief supervised ordinary crutch use. No recurrence by late afternoon.</p><p>Then:</p><p>This does not explain anything.</p><p>I stared at that sentence.</p><p>Crossed it out.</p><p>Wrote:</p><p>No conclusion yet.</p><p>Better.</p><p>I closed the notebook.</p><p>My thumb did not tingle.</p><p>I let it not.<br/></p></article>
- `light/104.html:16`: <article class="prose light-prose"><p>My thumb did not tingle in the morning.</p><p>This was disappointing.</p><p>Not medically.</p><p>Medically, it was excellent.</p><p>Scientifically, it was almost useless.</p><p>Emotionally, I wanted the thumb to do something interesting and was mature enough not to admit this to Hessa.</p><p>I wrote:</p><p>No tingling overnight. None on waking. Hip similar. Residual limb baseline. Hands fine.</p><p>I had no Hessa appointment.</p><p>I could ask Pessa to train.</p><p>I wanted to.</p><p>I also wanted to tell Jorren that I had shaped mana badly.</p><p>These wants competed for perhaps twelve seconds.</p><p>Jorren won because he would be more impressed.</p><p>This was not true.</p><p>That was why it was funny.</p><p>I found him at the Guild.</p><p>He was arguing with Alden about boots.</p><p>Not metaphorically.</p><p>Actual boots.</p><p>Alden had one foot on a bench and was pulling the laces tight enough to restrict future generations.</p><p>Jorren stood over two.”</p><p>Alden glanced down.</p><p>Then up.</p><p>He did not apologize.</p><p>Good.</p><p>I appreciated that too.</p><p>“Tam?” he asked.</p><p>I thought of my damaged left boot and the salvage hated that Pessa had spread.</p><p>We went to the market.</p><p>Jorren did not need a knife.</p><p>This became clear at the third stall.</p><p>He wanted a knife.</p><p>Different category.</p><p>His statement I distrusted professionally and understood personally.</p><p>He tried six.</p><p>Rejected two immediately.</p><p>Kept returning to the dark-handled one.</p><p>“Buy that one.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“You keep picking it up.”</p><p>“That doesn't mean it's best.”</p><p>“You are buying a food knife, not appointing a magistrate.”</p><p>“What if the other one is thumb.</p><p>Maybe.</p><p>I did not squeeze it.</p><p>Did not touch fingertips.</p><p>Did not flex repeatedly.</p><p>I simply noticed.</p><p>Jorren had picked up a knife.</p><p>He looked at stall.</p><p>I sat.</p><p>Annoying when friends became reasonable.</p><p>“How long?”</p><p>“Just started.”</p><p>“Pain?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Numb?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Cold?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“You hands.”</p><p>“So does he.”</p><p>“Yes, but apparently his are busy.”</p><p>I laughed.</p><p>Hessa did not.</p><p>We left.</p><p>Outside, Jorren said, “I like her.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“She gave me a knife.”</p><p>He did.</p><p>No revelation.</p><p>No speech.</p><p>Coins.</p><p>Knife.</p><p>A simple sheath because carrying an exposed kitchen blade through Carrow was apparently discouraged by civilization.</p><p>We walked back toward the Guild.</p><p>My thumb did not tingle.</p><p>I did not check it.</p><p>Jorren carried the knife like he had acquired a minor title.</p><p>“Worth it?” I asked.</p><p>“I haven't cut anything.”</p><p>“You already like it.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That may be enough.”</p><p>He glanced at me.</p><p>“Careful.”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“You almost sounded time.</p><p>Body fine.</p><p>Hessa had not prohibited physical training.</p><p>Thumb currently normal.</p><p>But if I went to Pessa, I would spend the whole session wondering whether the thumb dangerous.”</p><p>“Come supervise.”</p><p>“I am not qualified.”</p><p>“You have eaten food.”</p><p>“Extensively.”</p><p>“Exactly.”</p><p>I followed him.</p><p>My thumb remained a thumb.</p><p>For the moment, this was acceptable.<br/></p></article>

find out.”</p><p>“Could the old pattern be impossible to suppress?”</p><p>“We do not know.”</p><p>“Could it be useful?”</p><p>“Later question.”</p><p>“Could relearning involve replacing old badly.</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>I exhaled.</p><p>Not because I expected more.</p><p>Because maybe was not no.</p><p>Dangerous.</p><p>She saw that too.</p><p>“Do not build a future out of one failed thumb.”</p><p>“That is a cruel sentence.”</p><p>“It is accurate.”</p><p>I drank tea.</p><p>The excitement did not go away.</p><p>Neither did the irritation.</p><p>Good combination.</p><p>“What is next test?”</p><p>“Probably the same instruction.”</p><p>“Same thumb?”</p><p>“Probably.”</p><p>“Same position?”</p><p>“Probably seated.”</p><p>“Same copper?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>“Why not tomorrow?”</p><p>“I want a boring day between attempts.”</p><p>“Delayed effects.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then when?”</p><p>“Day after tomorrow.”</p><p>I stared.</p><p>“You are obsessed with boring days.”</p><p>“I am interested in delayed effects.”</p><p>“There were none before.”</p><p>“Before was draw only.”</p><p>Right.</p><p>This was different.</p><p>Tiny.</p><p>Still different.</p><p>“Can I train with Pessa tomorrow?”</p><p>“Medically, if you remain at baseline, I do not object to you asking her.”</p><p>“Same answer.”</p><p>“Same question.”</p><p>“Can I tell her I shaped?”</p><p>“You can tell her what happened.”</p><p>“She will say she doesn't care.”</p><p>“Probably.”</p><p>I smiled.</p><p>“Can I tell Jorren?”</p><p>Hessa looked confused.</p><p>“Why are you asking me?”</p><p>“I don't know.”</p><p>“You may tell your friend you failed to move mana into your thumb.”</p><p>“That wording is hostile.”</p><p>“It is accurate.”</p><p>I thought about Jorren's response.</p><p>Probably:</p><p>Good.</p><p>That was somehow irritating in advance.</p><p>“Can I write it down?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Paragraphs?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No table?”</p><p>She stared.</p><p>“Sorry.”</p><p>I finished the tea.</p><p>Hessa checked my hand once more.</p><p>Then:</p><p>“Stand.”</p><p>Both crutches.</p><p>Right foot.</p><p>Push.</p><p>No problem.</p><p>My right thumb tingled.</p><p>I froze.</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>She was immediately attentive.</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“Thumb tingling.”</p><p>“How much?”</p><p>“Very mild.”</p><p>“Pain?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Numb?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Cold?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She touched the thumb.</p><p>Then fingers.</p><p>Had me squeeze.</p><p>Release.</p><p>Touch each fingertip.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>“Still?”</p><p>“Yes. Less.”</p><p>She waited.</p><p>We waited.</p><p>The tingling faded.</p><p>“Gone.”</p><p>She wrote.</p><p>I looked at the notebook.</p><p>“Concerning?”</p><p>“Not currently.”</p><p>“Relevant?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Delayed effect?”</p><p>“Immediate minor effect.”</p><p>“Could be from gripping the crutch.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Could be from shaping.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Could be attention.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Useful.”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>I laughed.</p><p>She did not.</p><p>“Greg.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Report if it returns.”</p><p>“I will.”</p><p>“No self-test.”</p><p>“I will not.”</p><p>“No thumb experiments.”</p><p>“I will not.”</p><p>“No Barrier rehearsal.”</p><p>“I will not.”</p><p>“No trying to reproduce the wrist movement without mana as a magical exercise.”</p><p>I paused.</p><p>“That is very specific.”</p><p>“Because I know you.”</p><p>Fair.</p><p>I left.</p><p>Outside, I looked at my right thumb.</p><p>Not because I was testing it.</p><p>Because it was attached to my hand.</p><p>Important legal distinction.</p><p>I had shaped mana.</p><p>Badly.</p><p>Into the wrong place.</p><p>With an old reflex trying to take over.</p><p>Possibly.</p><p>One tiny deliberate failure.</p><p>I was so happy I nearly walked into a barrel.</p><p>The barrel did not care.</p><p>Carrow remained consistent.<br/></p></article>

better.”</p><p>I laughed.</p><p>Then watched.</p><p>No theory.</p><p>No notebook.</p><p>Just arrows.</p><p>Alden adjusted.</p><p>Lio corrected something in his shoulder.</p><p>Pessa corrected both.</p><p>I ate apple.</p><p>At one point, my phantom left foot felt planted.</p><p>Ordinary.</p><p>I noticed.</p><p>Did nothing.</p><p>Later it was gone.</p><p>No connection.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Lyssa found me near evening.</p><p>Not because I had summoned her.</p><p>She came through the Guild yard looking for someone else first.</p><p>A woman from the freight side waved to her.</p><p>Lyssa crossed over, spoke briefly, handed her a small wrapped bundle, accepted coins, then finally looked around and saw me.</p><p>Independent business.</p><p>Good.</p><p>She came over.</p><p>“You&#x27;re sitting.”</p><p>“Apparently suspicious.”</p><p>“To everyone.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>She looked at the practice target.</p><p>“Training?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Magic?”</p><p>“Earlier.”</p><p>Her eyes changed.</p><p>“How?”</p><p>“I shaped and failed to stop.”</p><p>“That sounds complicated.”</p><p>“It was.”</p><p>“Did it hurt?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Are you allowed?”</p><p>“One attempt. Supervised.”</p><p>“Hessa?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Did she look angry?”</p><p>“Normal face.”</p><p>Lyssa smiled.</p><p>“Then good.”</p><p>There it was.</p><p>Again.</p><p>I told her the short version.</p><p>She listened.</p><p>Not pretending to understand channel mechanics.</p><p>“What happens next?”</p><p>“No magic tomorrow.”</p><p>“You hate that.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then?”</p><p>“Assessment.”</p><p>“More stopping?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>She laughed before I could react.</p><p>Cruel.</p><p>“I hate that word.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>We walked out together.</p><p>Not a date.</p><p>Not declared.</p><p>She had finished work.</p><p>I was done watching arrows.</p><p>We were both hungry.</p><p>That was enough.</p><p>At the first food stall, she chose something with too much sauce.</p><p>I chose the same.</p><p>Bad strategy.</p><p>Good food.</p><p>We ate standing for her and sitting for me on a low wall.</p><p>Lyssa got sauce on one finger and wiped it on the paper wrapping.</p><p>“You&#x27;re staring.”</p><p>“At the food.”</p><p>“You&#x27;re terrible at lying.”</p><p>“I had a whole card chapter about this.”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“Nothing.”</p><p>She took another bite.</p><p>I looked at her, then at the street.</p><p>People were closing shutters one at a time. A cart rolled past with one wheel making a soft repeated click. Someone farther down the road was arguing about whether a basket belonged inside or outside a doorway.</p><p>Carrow did not care that I had shaped mana.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Lyssa finished first.</p><p>“You want mine?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You answered before I finished.”</p><p>“You were offering food.”</p><p>“I could have been asking whether you wanted the paper.”</p><p>“I would still have said yes eventually.”</p><p>She handed me the last two bites.</p><p>My hand stayed normal.</p><p>My residual limb stayed normal.</p><p>No spell had happened.</p><p>I had shaped mana and failed to stop it cleanly.</p><p>That was progress.</p><p>Not because failure was secretly success.</p><p>Because it was finally specific enough to be wrong.</p><p>I liked that.</p></article>

- `light/139.html:16`: <article class="prose light-prose"><p>Hessa had moved the towel. I noticed before I sat down. Not far. Perhaps two fingers toward the end of the table. I put both crutches against the wall and looked at it. Hessa was grinding something in a small stone bowl. The room smelled bitter and green, with something sharper underneath that caught in the back of my nose. Morning light came through the narrow window beside her shelves and made every suspended bit of herb dust unnecessarily visible.</p><p>"You moved the towel."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"It was wet."</p><p>I looked at her. She kept grinding.</p><p>"You replaced it."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"In a different position."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"It is farther down the table."</p><p>Hessa stopped. She looked at the towel. Then at me. Then back at the towel.</p><p>"It is a towel, Gregory."</p><p>"That is not an answer."</p><p>"It is the only answer you are getting before you sit down."</p><p>I sat. The cot creaked under me. Hessa resumed grinding. I looked at the towel. Yesterday I had performed in front of an audience. Today I was suspicious of folded linen. This seemed like a decline.</p><p>"How was the show?" Hessa asked.</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>"You know about the show?"</p><p>"I know you went."</p><p>"That is not the same thing."</p><p>"No."</p><p>She scraped the crushed leaves into a small paper fold. I waited. She did not ask again.</p><p>"Parts were good," I said.</p><p>"Mm."</p><p>"Parts were bad."</p><p>"Sounds like a show."</p><p>"You've been?"</p><p>"To shows?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"No. I've spent my entire life avoiding rooms with chairs."</p><p>I frowned. Hessa glanced at me.</p><p>"That was a joke."</p><p>"I know."</p><p>"You looked injured."</p><p>"I was determining whether you were mocking Teren."</p><p>"I don't know Teren."</p><p>"Then probably not."</p><p>She put the paper fold aside and washed the pestle in a basin. Water tapped against stone. Somewhere below us, a door opened hard enough to rattle the window, followed by a man's voice complaining about somebody's cart. Carrow was awake. I had slept badly. Not because of magic. That distinction mattered. I had spent too much of the night remembering an audience laughing. Also not laughing. The not laughing had been more educational. Possibly. I had no idea. Then there was the trip. Five days. Maybe six. East. Temporary.</p><p>There was an old municipal hall there with a roof I had wanted to see before I died the first time. That was a perfectly legitimate reason to travel. The theatre was also going. Coincidence. Mostly.</p><p>"Sleep?" Hessa asked.</p><p>"Enough."</p><p>"How much?"</p><p>I told her.</p><p>"Water?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Food?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Alcohol?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Pain?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Cramping?"</p><p>"Ordinary."</p><p>"Residual limb?"</p><p>"Baseline."</p><p>"Right hand?"</p><p>"Normal."</p><p>"Forearm?"</p><p>"Normal."</p><p>"Phantom?"</p><p>"Ordinary."</p><p>She dried her hands.</p><p>"You said ordinary very quickly."</p><p>"It is ordinary."</p><p>"You checked?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>That was not entirely true. I had noticed. Noticing was not checking. Probably. Hessa watched me for another moment, then wrote something.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Nothing."</p><p>"You wrote."</p><p>"I often do."</p><p>"What did you write?"</p><p>"That you answered too quickly."</p><p>"That contaminates the record."</p><p>"It is the record."</p><p>I disliked her profession. Hessa pulled the stool over and sat beside the cot. The copper strip was already on the small tray. So was charcoal, paper, and the same narrow measuring cord she had used before. No thread apparatus. Good. I had not expected it. I was still glad.</p><p>"What are we doing?"</p><p>"Drawing mana."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Then shaping."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Then reporting."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"And then?"</p><p>"We stop."</p><p>I stared at her.</p><p>"That is the entire assessment?"</p><p>"If nothing interesting happens."</p><p>"That is barely an assessment."</p><p>"You have become very difficult to impress."</p><p>"Nineteen draws."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Fifteen shaping attempts."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Three external attempts."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"And now we're going backward."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"We are doing something I could already do."</p><p>"That is not backward."</p><p>"It is not forward."</p><p>Hessa leaned over and tapped the paper with one finger.</p><p>"Last time you gave me a more detailed description of the neutral shape than you had before the directional tests."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"The neutral shape was not neutral in the way you assumed."</p><p>"I did not assume it was symmetrical."</p><p>"You drew it symmetrical."</p><p>"Because I thought it was."</p><p>"Excellent. We have located the assumption."</p><p>I shut my mouth. She continued.</p><p>"If your ordinary shaped state already has a more distinct wrist-side boundary, then a later report that the wrist-side boundary became more distinct under instruction means less than it would if the starting shape were even."</p><p>"It still changed."</p><p>"Perhaps."</p><p>"It did."</p><p>"You reported that it did."</p><p>I hated that sentence too. Hessa did not look pleased about saying it. That made it worse. She set my right forearm onto the folded towel. The position was familiar. Palm down, forearm supported, elbow free enough that I was not pressing hard into the table edge. I looked at the towel.</p><p>"It is different."</p><p>Hessa closed her eyes.</p><p>"Gregory."</p><p>"Two fingers."</p><p>"You may leave."</p><p>"I didn't say it invalidated the test."</p><p>"You are looking at cloth instead of your arm."</p><p>"I can do both."</p><p>"That is precisely the problem."</p><p>Fair. I looked at my arm. Hessa adjusted the copper strip.</p><p>"Minimal draw."</p><p>I breathed. Reached. Mana came. Not dramatically. It had stopped feeling dramatic several assessments ago, which was probably dangerous in its own way. There. Present. Contained. The copper responded.</p><p>"Confirmed," Hessa said.</p><p>I held. Right side normal. Hand normal. Thumb quiet. No motor urge. No cold. No pain. My left phantom foot existed somewhere below the cot, vague and familiar and completely uninvolved.</p><p>"Shape," Hessa said.</p><p>I formed the small alteration in the right forearm. No direction. No external reach. Just the shape. It gathered slowly enough that I could feel the temptation to help it. I did not. There.</p><p>"Hold."</p><p>I held.</p><p>"Report."</p><p>"Localized. Similar size to last time."</p><p>"Similar is interpretation. Edges."</p><p>Right. I closed my eyes. Not because I needed to. Because the room became less annoying.</p><p>"Wrist-side boundary is clearest."</p><p>Hessa said nothing.</p><p>"Upper edge less distinct. Elbow side softer. Lower edge..."</p><p>I waited.</p><p>"Lower edge is difficult."</p><p>"Meaning?"</p><p>"I can tell where I think it stops. I cannot tell whether I'm feeling the end of the shape or the point where my attention stops being useful."</p><p>"Good."</p><p>"That wasn't a success."</p><p>"It was a report."</p><p>Fine.</p><p>"Anything changing?"</p><p>I waited. The shape stayed. Or mostly stayed. The upper edge felt broader than it had at the start. I did not like that.</p><p>"Upper edge may be spreading."</p><p>"May?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Direction?"</p><p>"Not instructed."</p><p>"I asked what direction."</p><p>"Oh. Toward the outside of the forearm. Slightly."</p><p>"Other edges?"</p><p>"Wrist side still clearest. Elbow side soft. Lower unclear."</p><p>Hessa wrote. I could hear the charcoal moving. Scritch. Pause. Scritch. It was surprisingly irritating.</p><p>"Draw it," she said.</p><p>"With my left hand?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"My left hand draws badly."</p><p>"It drew badly last time."</p><p>"So we are preserving the variable."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>I opened my eyes. Hessa put the paper where I could reach it without moving my right forearm. I took the charcoal in my left hand. The first line looked like a potato.</p><p>"This is useless."</p><p>"Continue."</p><p>I drew the wrist-side edge darker. Then the upper edge. Then the softer elbow side. The lower boundary got a broken line because I did not trust it. Hessa watched the paper, not my face.</p><p>"Done?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Look at the prior one."</p><p>She turned over a sheet beside her ledger. My drawing from the last assessment. I looked between them. Oh. The wrist-side boundary was dark in both. The elbow side was soft in both. The upper edge was not identical, but it was close enough that I could not dismiss it as nothing. The lower edge on the old drawing had been cleaner. Or I had drawn it cleaner. Those were not the same fact.</p><p>"Again," I said.</p><p>"No."</p><p>"One more neutral shape."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Same setup."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Because you are already comparing."</p><p>"That is the point."</p><p>"Not while you are holding mana."</p><p>I looked at my right arm. Fuck.</p><p>"Return," Hessa said.</p><p>I reduced the shape. The wrist-side edge softened first. Again. Not completely. The center faded. Upper edge lingered. I continued the same return without separately correcting it.</p><p>"Report."</p><p>"Wrist side reduced. Center reduced. Upper edge remains clearer."</p><p>"Continue."</p><p>I did. The remaining edge softened. Then I reached the familiar ugly point where I could not tell whether something remained or whether I was searching for it because Hessa had asked me to.</p><p>"Uncertain."</p><p>"Hold draw."</p><p>I held the underlying mana. The shaped alteration was either gone or below my confidence.</p><p>"Copper?"</p><p>"Draw remains," Hessa said.</p><p>"Release."</p><p>I released. The mana went. Nothing jumped. Nothing hurt. Nothing moved outside me. No thread trembled. No revelation occurred. Hessa waited anyway. She checked my hand, wrist, forearm, breathing, residual limb, and the things she always checked even when I was increasingly convinced she could do half of it by glaring.</p><p>"Anything?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Stand."</p><p>I reached for the crutches. She watched me rise. Right foot planted. Hands loaded. Hips came forward. Normal. I settled.</p><p>"Anything?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Walk."</p><p>I went to the window and back. The room was not large enough to make this dignified.</p><p>"Anything?"</p><p>"My dignity is declining."</p><p>"Baseline."</p><p>I looked at her. She wrote it down.</p><p>"You did not."</p><p>"I did."</p><p>"Hessa."</p><p>She smiled without looking up. Barely. That was worse than laughter. I sat again. She put the two drawings side by side. They were not identical. They were also not very different. I leaned closer.</p><p>"If that's the ordinary geometry," I said, "then the directional tests are weaker."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Not gone."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Because there were changes after instruction."</p><p>"Reported changes."</p><p>"Yes, yes."</p><p>"And because the prior tests were not mapped this way before the instruction, we cannot compare their starting geometry at the same level of detail."</p><p>I stared at the pages. That annoyed me more than if she had simply said the tests were bad. Bad could be discarded. These were not bad. They were incomplete. Much worse.</p><p>"So we repeat them."</p><p>"Eventually."</p><p>"With a pre-map."</p><p>"Possibly."</p><p>"Same position."</p><p>"Possibly."</p><p>"Same towel."</p><p>Hessa looked at me.</p><p>"I will preserve the sacred towel."</p><p>"Thank you."</p><p>"I'll label it."</p><p>"That would actually help."</p><p>"I regret speaking."</p><p>She stacked the papers. I watched her. There was still something missing.</p><p>"What did today establish?"</p><p>"Establish is too strong."</p><p>"Fine. What did today support?"</p><p>"That your neutral shaped state may have a repeatable asymmetry under this setup."</p><p>"May."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Wrist-side boundary more distinct."</p><p>"In two detailed reports."</p><p>"And upper edge changes without directional instruction."</p><p>"In both assessments, though not identically."</p><p>"So anatomy?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Support pressure?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Arm position?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Natural magical geometry?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Expectation?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Day variation?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>I sighed.</p><p>"You really do have one answer."</p><p>"I have several. You keep asking questions with the same answer."</p><p>I looked at the two drawings again. Then I remembered the wagon. Not because it had anything to do with my forearm. Because it was leaving. Tomorrow, apparently. I had known that before coming here. I had not intended to bring it up until after the assessment. That was sensible. The assessment was medical and magical. The theatre was theatre. Separate.</p><p>"Hessa."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"I haven't asked."</p><p>"You changed your voice."</p><p>I stared at her.</p><p>"What does that mean?"</p><p>"You have an administrative question."</p><p>"I do not have an administrative voice."</p><p>"You absolutely do."</p><p>I considered objecting. That would delay the question.</p><p>"The theatre is leaving Carrow tomorrow."</p><p>Hessa's hand stopped over the ledger.</p><p>"For how long?"</p><p>"Five days. Maybe six."</p><p>"Where?"</p><p>I told her. She knew the town. Of course she did. Hessa knew every place within a week's travel where somebody had once broken a wrist badly.</p><p>"Why are you telling me?"</p><p>"Because I might go."</p><p>"Might?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>She waited. I disliked silence when other people used it deliberately.</p><p>"I want to see the municipal hall," I said.</p><p>Hessa nodded.</p><p>"The roof was rebuilt twice."</p><p>"Mm."</p><p>"The original load paths are strange."</p><p>"I'm sure."</p><p>"And the theatre is performing there."</p><p>"An extraordinary coincidence."</p><p>I looked at her. She remained completely serious.</p><p>"I would be traveling with them."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"There would be wagons."</p><p>"I know what theatres use."</p><p>"Do you?"</p><p>"No. But I know what roads use."</p><p>Fair.</p><p>"I wouldn't test anything independently."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"I wouldn't draw."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"I wouldn't shape."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"I wouldn't cast."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"I know."</p><p>"I am enjoying this part."</p><p>I shifted on the cot.</p><p>"What I am asking is whether going changes your restrictions."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>My stomach tightened. Hessa closed the ledger.</p><p>"You will be somewhere else."</p><p>"That is not what I meant."</p><p>"It is what I mean. If you are injured, sick, exhausted, or develop a new symptom, I am not there."</p><p>"I understand."</p><p>"Do you?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"You said you slept enough this morning."</p><p>"I did."</p><p>"You slept badly."</p><p>I stopped. She had not asked whether I slept well. Only how much. Annoying woman.</p><p>"I slept enough badly."</p><p>"That sentence is why I worry about you."</p><p>"You don't worry about me."</p><p>"No."</p><p>She began wrapping the charcoal in cloth.</p><p>"I simply arrange my professional decisions around the possibility that you will do something stupid."</p><p>"That sounds like worry."</p><p>"It is risk management."</p><p>She tied the cloth twice. Too tightly for something she did not care about. I did not mention it.</p><p>"So can I go?"</p><p>"I don't control where you travel."</p><p>"That is evasive."</p><p>"It is accurate. I control what magical work I supervise and what I clear you to do."</p><p>"And?"</p><p>"And you remain uncleared for independent draw, shaping, casting, Barrier work, external testing, or whatever clever category you invent because you think it isn't technically one of those."</p><p>"I wasn't going to."</p><p>Hessa looked at me.</p><p>"I wasn't."</p><p>She kept looking.</p><p>"I probably wasn't."</p><p>"Better."</p><p>I rubbed my palm against my trouser leg.</p><p>"If I go, when is the next assessment?"</p><p>"When you return."</p><p>"That could be six days."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"We've been working on a shorter cadence."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"So the gap changes the sequence."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>I waited. Hessa waited back.</p><p>"You're not going to tell me not to go."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Do you want me to?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Then this is an odd complaint."</p><p>"I expected you to object."</p><p>"I object to unsupervised magic. I object to you converting uncertainty into permission. I object to you pretending symptoms don't count because they interfere with your plans."</p><p>"I don't do that."</p><p>She looked at me. Fine.</p><p>"Not consistently."</p><p>"Better."</p><p>She stood and carried the bowl to the shelf. I looked at the drawings again. Six days without an assessment. Possibly. Five. The theatre had chairs in other towns. Apparently. Also shopkeepers. I could stay. That would be easier. Known room. Known stairs. Hessa. Guild. Pessa. Lyssa. Jorren. Work if it appeared. Theatre again when they came back, assuming they came back when expected. Nothing required me to leave Carrow. That was important. I was not being forced onto a road. I was not fleeing anything.</p><p>I was not chasing work I needed to survive. I was not even formally part of the troupe. There were excellent reasons not to go.</p><p>"Hessa."</p><p>She turned.</p><p>"If I travel tomorrow, is today the last assessment before I leave?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>I nodded.</p><p>"That is irritating."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>She came back to the table and pushed the newer drawing toward me.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Take it."</p><p>I stared.</p><p>"You keep the records."</p><p>"I have the record."</p><p>She tapped her ledger.</p><p>"Take the drawing."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"So when you spend six days thinking about it, you can at least think about the thing you actually reported."</p><p>I picked it up.</p><p>"That sounds like permission to analyze it."</p><p>"No magic."</p><p>"I said analyze."</p><p>"No reconstructing the sensation."</p><p>"I can't promise not to remember my own arm."</p><p>"You know the difference."</p><p>I did. Mostly. I folded the paper once. Hessa immediately said, "Don't." I unfolded it.</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"You just folded through the wrist boundary."</p><p>I stared at her.</p><p>"You said the drawing isn't independent evidence."</p><p>"It isn't."</p><p>"Then why does the fold matter?"</p><p>"Because now I have to wonder whether you will later remember the fold as part of the line."</p><p>I looked at the charcoal mark. Then at her.</p><p>"That is extremely annoying."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>She gave me a scrap of stiff paper to carry it between. I slid the drawing inside. At the door I collected my crutches.</p><p>"Hessa."</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"If I go east, and nothing changes, I come back and we continue?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Same restrictions."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Same question?"</p><p>"We'll see."</p><p>I opened the door.</p><p>"And Gregory?"</p><p>I looked back. She had already reopened the ledger.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Go because you want to go."</p><p>I frowned.</p><p>"I told you. The municipal hall."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"The roof is genuinely interesting."</p><p>"I believe you."</p><p>"And I'm useful to the theatre."</p><p>"I didn't ask."</p><p>"They need the sword."</p><p>"Gregory."</p><p>"And possibly the Shopkeeper."</p><p>"Leave my office."</p><p>I did. The street outside was brighter than I expected. A produce cart blocked half the lane, and two women were arguing over whether a basket of onions belonged to one of them or to a shop three doors down. Someone had hung wet shirts from an upper window. They snapped in the breeze above the street like surrender flags nobody respected. I tucked Hessa's drawing safely inside my coat. The theatre left tomorrow. I had an entire day to decide whether I was going. I turned west.</p></article>
