No knife. No water. No Arlo. Spoon. Dish. Myself. That last resource was unfortunately available. I extended one finger toward the shard. Antonius slapped my hand away. I stared at him. He stared back.</p><p>"Did you just hit me?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"I'm an adult."</p><p>"Then act like one."</p><p>"I was going to touch the dish."</p><p>"No, you weren't," Antonius said.</p><p>He was correct. I disliked this phase of our relationship.</p><p>"Mana," I said.</p><p>His expression flattened.</p><p>"Your teacher cleared you to test unknown dungeon material?"</p><p>"Not exactly."</p><p>"Then we're not using mana on it here."</p><p>"A Barrier between me and the shard could..."</p><p>"After someone who knows the material tells us what it reacts to."</p><p>"Technically I learned it decades..." </p><p>I stopped. Antonius's eyes sharpened.</p><p>"Decades?"</p><p>"Conceptually." He waited. </p><p>I smiled. </p><p>He did not.</p><p>"Long story."</p><p>"You are nineteen."</p><p>"Very observant."</p><p>"Greg."</p><p>"Barrier. Tiny. No contact. I want to see whether it reacts to nearby mana."</p><p>"How?"</p><p>That was the useful question. I looked down. How? Old me would have flooded it gently and watched the response. Current me could barely flood a biscuit. That might actually be an advantage. A large mana input could activate something. A tiny one might reveal sensitivity without supplying enough energy to do much. Might. Hessa would have objected to the word might.</p><p>Hessa was not here. That thought immediately made the plan worse. I sighed.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"I just realized my teacher would say no."</p><p>"Then no."</p><p>"That's not how expertise works."</p><p>"It is when the expert isn't here and the idiot is."</p><p>"I'm not an idiot."</p><p>"Then why did you tell me she'd say no?"</p><p>Because apparently I had begun developing a conscience with Hessa's voice. Unfortunate. I set the spoon down.</p><p>"Fine." </p><p>Antonius looked surprised. That annoyed me enough to nearly reverse the decision. Instead I leaned closer without touching anything.</p><p>"What did the salvager say?"</p><p>"About?"</p><p>"This."</p><p>"Found it in a chamber."</p><p>"What kind?"</p><p>"Stone."</p><p>"Everything in a dungeon is in a stone chamber."</p><p>"He didn't describe the architecture for your pleasure."</p><p>"Was it attached to anything?" Antonius opened his ledger. </p><p>I smiled.</p><p>"You wrote it down."</p><p>"I write down collateral."</p><p>"This isn't collateral."</p><p>"I write down things people bring me when I may buy them."</p><p>"Read."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Because I want to know what you see without being told what he saw." </p><p>I sat back. There it was. A test. Not cruel. Useful. Antonius had started separating information. I felt an absurd little pulse of pride.</p><p>"You are getting better."</p><p>"At what?"</p><p>"Me."</p><p>His face did something I could not quite read. Then it disappeared.</p><p>"Work," Antonius said.</p><p>I looked at the shard.</p><p>Fine.</p><p>What could I observe? Color. Structure. Hardness, roughly. No obvious smell beyond mineral sharpness. No visible residue. Black inclusion. Translucent green matrix. I moved the spoon around it. The underside had a duller surface. Broken?</p><p>No.</p><p>One face was irregular but rounded. Growth surface. The opposite face was sharp. Fracture.</p><p>"So it grew on something." Antonius said nothing.</p><p>Good.</p><p>I rotated it. The black veins widened toward the rounded face. Not random. They converged. I leaned closer. The black material was not distributed through the green. It originated from one side and branched inward. Like roots. Or contamination. Or the green had grown around it.</p><p>"Was the black part attached to the wall?"</p><p>Antonius's eyes changed. Small. There.</p><p>"Yes," Antonius said.</p><p>I grinned.</p><p>"Good."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"I don't know."</p><p>His expression became hostile again.</p><p>"Still good."</p><p>I traced the shape in the air. Green growth around black substrate. A healer's tent. Green powder. Not the black part. Maybe the green was medicinal. Maybe the black was toxic. Too easy. Memory loved creating stories after the fact. I needed a test. Not a dangerous test. A comparison.</p><p>"Do you have more?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Did he?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"How much?" </p><p>Antonius did not answer.</p><p>"Enough that value matters."</p><p>"Everything's value matters."</p><p>"Enough that you are asking me instead of selling it as pretty glass." He tapped the ledger once.</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"How much?"</p><p>"Several sacks." I went still. Several sacks changed the problem. A curiosity could be worthless. Several sacks could become a market. Or a disposal cost.</p><p>"Did he bring the black material separately?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"All veined?"</p><p>"Most."</p><p>"Most?" I asked.</p><p>Antonius looked annoyed.</p><p>Excellent.</p><p>"Some pieces were clear green?"</p><p>"A few."</p><p>There. My memory moved. Not a name. A motion. Someone at the healer's table snapping green material. Sorting. Black pieces thrown into a bucket. Green into the mortar. The bucket had a lid. Why a lid? Smell? Contact? Mana? I closed my eyes. The memory dissolved when I chased it.</p><p>"Fuck."</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"I almost had it."</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Someone sorting this." Antonius became very still. Not because he believed me. Because he had learned that when I said things like that, there was usually money nearby.</p><p>"Where?"</p><p>"Later."</p><p>"When?"</p><p>"Years."</p><p>"How many?" </p><p>I opened my eyes.</p><p>"I don't know."</p><p>"Who?"</p><p>"I don't know."</p><p>"What was it used for?"</p><p>"I don't know."</p><p>"Useful."</p><p>"Very."</p><p>He leaned back. I could see him evaluating whether the strange young debtor in front of him was a prophet, liar, lunatic, or simply someone with an unusually broad education and terrible boundaries. I had spent weeks helping him avoid settling on an answer.</p><p>"Green part went into a mortar," I said. "Black part went into a covered bucket."</p><p>"Covered?"</p><p>"I think."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"I don't know."</p><p>"Was the green medicine?"</p><p>"Probably."</p><p>"Probably?"</p><p>"Healer's tent."</p><p>"Could have been poison."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Could have been dye."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Could have been cleaning powder."</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Could have been anything."</p><p>"Now you're understanding memory." </p><p>Antonius stared. I had said too much again. Not enough to reveal the Chronoclast. Enough to be strange. Strange was becoming expensive. </p><p>I picked up the spoon.</p><p>"We need someone who knows healing materials."</p><p>"Arlo?"</p><p>"Wrong craft."</p><p>"Apothecary?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Who?"</p><p>That was the problem. I knew excellent healers. Future healers. People who would eventually know enough to identify rare dungeon reagents by smell. At nineteen, some of them were children. One was probably not born. One had not yet lost the eye that made him famous, which was a sentence I did not enjoy knowing. Present Carrow? I searched memory. Shops. Guild suppliers.</p><p>Names. Nothing clean. Then a face. Round spectacles. Permanent irritation. A woman who once charged me triple because I had bled on her floor. Was that Carrow? Maybe. Name. Name.</p><p>"Meret," I said.</p><p>Antonius said, "Meret what?"</p><p>"I don't know."</p><p>"Excellent expert."</p><p>"Apothecary. Maybe south market."</p><p>"Maybe?"</p><p>"I haven't seen her in a long time."</p><p>"How long?" </p><p>I looked at him. </p><p>He smiled. Bastard.</p><p>"Long enough." </p><p>Antonius stood.</p><p>"Where are you going?"</p><p>"South market."</p><p>"Now?"</p><p>"You wanted value."</p><p>"I wanted an answer."</p><p>"Answers live in places."</p><p>"I have work."</p><p>"Then stay." </p><p>He looked at the green shard. Then at me. Then put the shard into a small wooden box. </p><p>I held out my hand. </p><p>He did not give it to me.</p><p>"You're coming."</p><p>"I thought you had work."</p><p>"I've met you."</p><p>"That doesn't answer the question."</p><p>"It answers mine."</p><p>We went to the south market. Meret was not there. There was an apothecary. There was a woman with round spectacles. She was not Meret. She was also approximately sixty years old, which meant unless my memory had become creative in new and upsetting ways, she would have been about one hundred when I knew her. Possible. Unlikely. Her sign read NERA VOSS - APOTHECARY &amp; PHYSIC.</p><p>I stood outside. </p><p>Antonius said, "Meret?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"You said round spectacles."</p><p>"Many people have spectacles."</p><p>"You said south market."</p><p>"I said maybe."</p><p>"You are very expensive for a man who says maybe this often."</p><p>"You paid me six silver once."</p><p>"Exactly."</p><p>I looked through the window. Shelves. Dried herbs. Ceramic jars. Glass bottles. A copper distillation coil in the back. Clean. Organized. Two customers. One assistant. Good enough.</p><p>"We ask." </p><p>Antonius did not move.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"You ask."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Because this was your idea."</p><p>"You're the one holding the box."</p><p>He gave me the box. Ah. Punishment through responsibility. I entered. The shop smelled like bitterroot, alcohol, dried flowers, and money pretending to be health. Nera Voss looked up from a scale.</p><p>"Wait."</p><p>I waited. Antonius entered behind me and immediately became invisible in the way competent men sometimes did when they wanted to watch. Not physically. Socially. He stood near a shelf and became a customer. I hated recognizing my own tricks in other people. Nera finished weighing a dark powder, folded the paper, tied it, took payment, and looked at me.</p><p>"Yes?"</p><p>"I have a material I'd like identified."</p><p>"Guild assay office."</p><p>"Closed?"</p><p>"Open."</p><p>"Expensive?"</p><p>"Appropriately."</p><p>"Slow?"</p><p>"Also appropriately." She looked past me to the next customer. </p><p>I put the box on the counter.</p><p>"Recovered from a dungeon."</p><p>That got half a second. Enough.</p><p>"Guild assay."</p><p>"Several sacks."</p><p>Now I had her. Not because she was greedy. Because several sacks meant repeat supply. Professionals liked repeat supply. She opened the box. Her face did not change. Then it did. Barely. Recognition. I smiled. She closed the box.</p><p>"Where?"</p><p>"That's not part of identification."</p><p>"It is if you want identification."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Because half the names for dungeon reagents are location names."</p><p>Fair. I glanced at Antonius. He did nothing. Of course.</p><p>"What can you tell me without origin?"</p><p>"Nothing for free."</p><p>"Price?"</p><p>"Two silver." I laughed. </p><p>She looked offended.</p><p>"To look?"</p><p>"To identify."</p><p>"You already recognized it."</p><p>"Then you don't need me."</p><p>Good.</p><p>I liked her.</p><p>"One silver if you cannot identify it."</p><p>"Two."</p><p>"One now, one if you can give us a usable name, handling warning, and ordinary buyer."</p><p>She looked at me. Then Antonius. Ah. She had found the adult. Antonius said, "One and one." Traitor. Nera held out her hand. Antonius did not move. I paid. Of course I paid. One silver. My six silver had briefly existed. Arlo had three. Now Nera had one. Money was apparently a substance that became unstable near me. She reopened the box.</p><p>"Don't touch the black."</p><p>Memory slammed into place hard enough that I actually laughed. Nera looked up. Antonius did not. He had the expression of a man watching a debt become interesting.</p><p>"Why?" I asked.</p><p>Nera reached beneath the counter and pulled on thin treated gloves. Not leather. Waxed gut, maybe. She lifted the shard.</p><p>"The green growth is called vairglass by salvagers. Apothecaries call the cleaned material vair resin, though it isn't resin."</p><p>"Medicinal?"</p><p>"Sometimes."</p><p>"For?"</p><p>"Depends on preparation."</p><p>"That's not an answer."</p><p>"It is the answer you're buying for one silver." </p><p>I grinned. </p><p>She turned the shard toward the light.</p><p>"The black is deadroot."</p><p>"Plant?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Fungal?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"What is it?"</p><p>"We don't know."</p><p>Excellent.</p><p>Nera frowned at me.</p><p>"Why are you pleased?"</p><p>"Because I didn't know either."</p><p>"That is a low standard."</p><p>"You'd like my teacher." Antonius made a sound that might have been a cough. Nera continued.</p><p>"Vairglass forms around deadroot deposits in some old dungeon growths. The green material can be processed. The black contaminant causes fever, numbness, vomiting, and sometimes mana shock if powdered or heated."</p><p>There it was. Covered bucket. Not because the black part was precious. Because healers did not want contaminated dust in a tent.</p><p>"Contact?"</p><p>"Usually skin is fine if intact."</p><p>"Usually?"</p><p>"Don't lick it."</p><p>"I wasn't going to," I said.</p><p>Antonius said, "He was."</p><p>"I was not."</p><p>Nera looked between us.</p><p>"I don't care." </p><p>I pointed at the black vein.</p><p>"Mana-active?"</p><p>"Both are."</p><p>"How?"</p><p>"Guild assay."</p><p>"Does the black react more strongly?"</p><p>"Guild assay."</p><p>"Does the green?"</p><p>"Guild assay."</p><p>"Can the green be used without grinding?"</p><p>"Some preparations dissolve it. Some powder it. Some heat it after cleaning."</p><p>"Cleaning how?"</p><p>"That costs more."</p><p>"How much?"</p><p>"Depends what you want."</p><p>There. The shape of the market. Not treasure. A processing problem. The raw material had value only if separated well enough for an apothecary to trust it. I thought of Arlo.</p><p>No.</p><p>Stop. Arlo had a regulator problem. Do not give Arlo another life. I almost laughed. Nera noticed.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Personal growth."</p><p>"Somewhere else." </p><p>Antonius stepped forward.</p><p>"Value raw," Antonius said.</p><p>Nera looked at him.</p><p>"Origin?" He gave her the dungeon name. </p><p>I did not recognize it. That bothered me. Not every dungeon mattered.</p><p>Good.</p><p>The world remained larger than my memory. Nera considered.</p><p>"How much?"</p><p>"Several sacks."</p><p>"Mostly like this."</p><p>"Black-heavy?"</p><p>"Mixed."</p><p>"Dry?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Stored how?"</p><p>"Sacks."</p><p>Nera closed her eyes briefly.</p><p>"Not anymore."</p><p>Antonius's face changed.</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Friction. Dust. If the black crumbles and the sacks are moved, you're spreading deadroot powder." </p><p>I looked at Antonius. </p><p>He looked at me.</p><p>"Where are the sacks?"</p><p>"Warehouse."</p><p>"People?"</p><p>"Working."</p><p>"Move them."</p><p>"No." </p><p>I blinked. </p><p>Nera blinked. Antonius said, "If moving them creates dust, we don't move them until I know how." Oh.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Very good. I had already been halfway out the door. Old Greg solved danger by acting faster. Antonius had refused to let urgency choose the method. I hated when he was better than me at something in front of witnesses. Nera nodded.</p><p>"Wet cloth over mouth and nose. No sweeping. No shaking sacks. Keep flame away. Put each sack into a rigid bin if you have them. Slowly."</p><p>"Workers?"</p><p>"Anyone with numb fingers, metallic taste, fever, nausea, or mana tremor goes to a physic."</p><p>"Mana tremor?"</p><p>"Uncontrolled channel flutter."</p><p>My wrist suddenly felt very noticeable. I had not touched it. I had almost used mana near it. Hessa would kill me. After Nera saved me. Then Hessa might resurrect me to explain why. Antonius said, "Can you inspect the lot?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Price?" Antonius asked.</p><p>"Half gold."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Then poison your warehouse."</p><p>"Three silver."</p><p>"Six."</p><p>"Four."</p><p>"Five and you provide handling."</p><p>"Five and I tell your workers what not to do."</p><p>"Done."</p><p>They shook hands. I stared. Nera looked at me.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"You charged me one silver to say deadroot."</p><p>"You asked badly," Nera said.</p><p>Antonius smiled. </p><p>I pointed at him.</p><p>"Don't encourage her." </p><p>He took the box. Outside, </p><p>I said, "I want my silver back."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"You got the answer."</p><p>"I paid five."</p><p>"You paid after my silver created the market."</p><p>"Your silver bought you an education."</p><p>"That is something poor people say when they lose money."</p><p>"You are poor."</p><p>"Temporarily."</p><p>"Consistently."</p><p>We walked faster. Not running. Antonius did not run. That was becoming another thing I noticed. He accelerated the system around him instead. At the warehouse, he did not shout about poison. He did not tell everyone a dangerous dungeon substance might be leaking through sacks near their flour, cloth, tools, and lungs. He walked in. Looked. Found the salvager.</p><p>Asked exactly where the sacks had been placed. Then he cleared the nearest work area for a "fragile inventory check." People complained. He paid two men for the lost hour. They stopped complaining. I watched.</p><p>"You knew they'd panic."</p><p>"People hear poison and become stupid."</p><p>"People hear danger and move."</p><p>"Usually badly."</p><p>Nera arrived twenty minutes later with gloves, cloth masks, two jars, waxed paper, and an assistant who looked terrified of her. The sacks were in a back storage bay. Six of them. Of course I wanted to see. Of course Antonius blocked the doorway.</p><p>"I'm helping."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"I identified it."</p><p>"Nera identified it."</p><p>"I identified that she could identify it."</p><p>"Congratulations."</p><p>"I know what the black part does."</p><p>"After she told you."</p><p>"I remembered first."</p><p>"After she told you."</p><p>"Simultaneously."</p><p>"Outside."</p><p>Nera looked over.</p><p>"He can stay if he wears this."</p><p>She threw me a cloth. I smiled at Antonius. He looked betrayed by professional disagreement. I tied the cloth over my mouth. Nera inspected the sacks one by one. No dramatic glow. No monster egg. No hidden curse. Just material. That was somehow better. The first sack contained mostly green chunks with thin black veins. The second was worse. The third had loose black grit at the bottom.</p><p>Nera stopped.</p><p>"That one doesn't move." Antonius said, "Why?"</p><p>"Bag's torn inside."</p><p>"Can it be salvaged?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"How?"</p><p>"Rigid container. Damp cloth. Scoop pieces individually. Don't pour." I looked at the spoon still sticking out of Antonius's coat pocket. He saw me look.</p><figure class="chapter-art scene-illustration"><img alt="Hazard Becomes Process" decoding="async" loading="lazy" onerror="this.closest('figure').remove()" src="../visual/chapter_art/012/v28_c12_s03_hazard-becomes-process.png"/></figure><p>"No."</p><p>I laughed into the cloth. The salvager arrived halfway through the inspection. His name was Corven. I knew that because Antonius used it. I did not recognize him from the future. He was broad, sun-browned, missing the tip of one ear, and furious.</p><p>"What are you doing?" </p><p>Antonius stepped out of the bay.</p><p>"Protecting your sale."</p><p>"My men packed that."</p><p>"Badly."</p><p>Corven looked at Nera.</p><p>"Who is she?"</p><p>"Apothecary."</p><p>His anger shifted. Not gone. Focused.</p><p>"Vair?"</p><p>Nera looked at him.</p><p>"You knew?"</p><p>"We thought."</p><p>"You thought and put deadroot in cloth sacks?"</p><p>"We didn't know the black was deadroot."</p><p>"Then you didn't know it was vair."</p><p>Corven's jaw worked.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Not a fool. Embarrassed. Different problem. Antonius said, "How much more is there?" Corven hesitated. I felt the answer before he gave it.</p><p>"A lot."</p><p>Every part of me woke up. Antonius noticed. He pointed at me without looking.</p><p>"No."</p><p>"I didn't say anything."</p><p>"Your entire body said dungeon."</p><p>Corven looked at me.</p><p>"Who is he?"</p><p>"Debt."</p><p>"Consultant," I said.</p><p>"Debt," Antonius repeated.</p><p>"Paid consultant."</p><p>"Occasionally."</p><p>Corven looked between us and decided not to ask. Smart man.</p><p>"How much?" Antonius asked.</p><p>"Chamber wall was covered."</p><p>Nera's assistant stopped moving. Nera did not.</p><p>"Covered how?" she asked.</p><p>"Sheets. Growths. Some clear. Some black."</p><p>"Depth?"</p><p>"Finger. Sometimes more."</p><p>"How large is the chamber?"</p><p>Corven spread his hands.</p><p>"Twenty paces? Thirty?"</p><p>I forgot to breathe. Not because of money. A chamber. Dungeon growth. Unknown supply. Handling hazard. Processing. Access. A bounded problem with stone walls around it. I wanted it so badly I could taste it. Not the vairglass. The dungeon. Antonius turned his head slowly toward me.</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Again, I have not spoken."</p><p>"You are vibrating."</p><p>"I am standing still."</p><p>"Internally."</p><p>Corven laughed. I liked him less. Nera said, "If it's a stable deposit, there's money." Antonius stopped looking at me.</p><p>"How much?"</p><p>"Raw? Less than you're hoping."</p><p>"Processed?"</p><p>"More than I can buy."</p><p>"Who can?"</p><p>"Guild suppliers. Military physickers. Two larger apothecary houses. Maybe alchemists, depending on grade."</p><p>"Price."</p><p>"Clean green, maybe eight to twelve silver a pound in small quantities. Less in bulk."</p><p>Corven swore. I did the calculation. Then stopped myself. Sacks were not pounds of clean green. Black contamination. Loss during processing. Labor. Transport. Dungeon access. Risk. Market depth. Antonius had infected me.</p><p>Good.</p><p>"Raw mixed?" I asked.</p><p>Nera shrugged.</p><p>"One silver a pound if I trust the source and contamination is low. Maybe less. Black-heavy, I don't buy."</p><p>Corven's excitement died. There. Future knowledge did not turn a dungeon wall into gold. It turned it into a supply chain. Much less romantic. Much more useful. Antonius asked, "Cleaning method?" Nera smiled.</p><p>"That costs."</p><p>"How much?"</p><p>"For commercial handling?"</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Two gold."</p><p>Corven laughed. Antonius did not. I looked at the material. Green around black. Separate without grinding the black. Manual sorting worked for healers because they were processing handfuls. Several sacks? A chamber wall? You needed a process. Break the green away from the black without pulverizing either. Different hardness? Different fracture? Different response to heat?</p><p>Water? Mana? Arlo...</p><p>No.</p><p>Not Arlo. Maybe.</p><p>No.</p><p>I physically pressed my lips together under the cloth. Antonius saw.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Nothing."</p><p>"That's your face for something."</p><p>"I am practicing restraint."</p><p>"Poorly."</p><p>Nera said, "If you're thinking of crushing it, don't."</p><p>"I wasn't," I said.</p><p>I had been.</p><p>"Grinding mixed material is how people poison themselves."</p><p>"What about fracture?" </p><p>She looked at me.</p><p>"Meaning?"</p><p>"The green grows around the deadroot. If their fracture behavior differs, you might separate larger pieces mechanically before any fine processing."</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Water?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Heat?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>That answer was fast.</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Deadroot dust gets worse when heated."</p><p>"Worse how?"</p><p>"More reactive."</p><p>"Mana?" </p><p>She stared.</p><p>"Guild assay." </p><p>I laughed. She was going to make money off me eventually. </p><p>Antonius said, "What do you need to test separation?" Nera thought.</p><p>"A safe yard. Water. Covered bins. Hammers. Screens. Gloves. Two workers who listen."</p><p>"How long?"</p><p>"Half day to learn whether the obvious methods work."</p><p>"Price?"</p><p>"Eight silver."</p><p>Corven said, "I'll pay half." Antonius looked at him.</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"It's my material."</p><p>"You owe me two gold."</p><p>"Which I can pay if this sells."</p><p>There. Antonius's face became very still. Not greedy. Structural. I watched him see the shape. Corven had already repaid three of five gold. The remaining debt was secured. The new material could produce additional value. But only if someone paid to learn how to handle it. Antonius could spend four silver to improve the probability of repayment and potentially create a new trade relationship.</p><p>That was his kind of bet.</p><p>"Half," Antonius said.</p><p>"I'll..."</p><p>"No," Antonius said.</p><p>"I didn't finish."</p><p>"You were going to invest."</p><p>"I was going to offer labor." </p><p>He paused. That was different. </p><p>I smiled.</p><p>"What labor?"</p><p>"Testing."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Observation."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Documentation." </p><p>Antonius looked at Nera. She looked at me.</p><p>"Can you write?" Nera asked.</p><p>I was offended.</p><p>"Yes."</p><p>"Legibly?"</p><p>Less offended.</p><p>"Usually." Antonius said, "No mana." </p><p>I opened my mouth.</p><p>"No magic," Antonius said.</p><p>I closed it.</p><p>"No experiments she doesn't approve."</p><p>"Define experiment."</p><p>"Greg."</p><p>Nera said, "He can write." Antonius looked at me. I could feel the boundary forming. A job. Not my life. Not my company. Not my dungeon. A half day. Record what happens. Ask useful questions. Do not acquire a processing enterprise. Do not recruit Arlo. Do not cast Barrier at poisonous dungeon material. I hated how much easier the world became when someone else built the fence.</p><p>"Fine," I said.</p><p>Antonius narrowed his eyes.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"You agreed too quickly."</p><p>"I'm growing."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"People keep saying that."</p><p>"No one says that."</p><p>"Hessa implied it."</p><p>"Did she?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Tomorrow morning," Nera said. "West yard behind my shop."</p><p>Corven nodded. </p><p>I nodded. </p><p>Antonius said, "You work for me tomorrow morning."</p><p>"I know."</p><p>"This counts."</p><p>"Excellent."</p><p>"Do not say that."</p><p>The next morning, I discovered that vairglass was less interesting when wet. Most things are. Nera had set up three shallow bins in the yard. One dry. One with water. One with a weak vinegar solution that made the entire place smell like pickled feet. Corven brought a small sack. Antonius brought himself. I brought paper. And, because history enjoys humiliating men who become too pleased with their own symbolism, a spoon.</p><p>Antonius saw it.</p><p>"Is that mine?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Where did you get it?"</p><p>"Bought it."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Professional equipment."</p><p>Nera said, "If either of you wastes my morning, leave." We worked. Not dramatically. That mattered. The first method was hand sorting. Slow. Safe enough. Bad economics. The second was soaking. The green material changed slightly after twenty minutes. Not dissolving. The surface became slick. The black did not. Interesting. Nera scraped the boundary with a wooden pick.</p><p>A thin layer separated.</p><p>"Again," I said. </p><p>She did. The green peeled away from one black vein in a translucent flake. Corven leaned closer. Antonius did not. He had learned about dust. I wrote:</p><p>WATER - SURFACE SOFTENS? BOUNDARY RELEASES.</p><p>Nera corrected me.</p><p>"Not softens."</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Feels the same."</p><p>"Then lubricates?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Swells?"</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>"Reaction?"</p><p>"Maybe," I said.</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>"You are enjoying this."</p><p>"Two gold for the process."</p><p>"We haven't bought it."</p><p>"You will."</p><p>Antonius said, "Keep testing." The vinegar did almost nothing useful. A light hammer tap fractured the green unpredictably. A second shattered a piece and made Nera swear at Corven. We stopped that. Screens were useless at the current size. Then I noticed something. The black veins were not just structurally different. Water collected along them. Not much. A thin dark line.</p><p>Surface tension? Texture? I moved closer.</p><p>"Can I use the spoon?"</p><p>Nera looked at the spoon.</p><p>"To do what?"</p><p>"Press the green beside the vein. Not the black."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"I want to see whether the boundary fails under sideways pressure," I said.</p><p>Nera considered, then handed me gloves. Antonius said, "No mana."</p><p>"I know."</p><p>I pressed. Nothing. More. The spoon slipped. The shard rotated. I stopped. Wrong angle. I repositioned it. The old version of me would have solved this with magic. Tiny Barrier. Perfectly placed. Pressure exactly where needed. Current me had a spoon.</p><p>Good.</p><p>I pressed again, not down. Across. A thin green flake popped away. Everyone stopped. I stared. Nera picked up the flake with tongs. Mostly clean. Tiny black trace at one edge.</p><p>"Again," she said.</p><p>I smiled. Antonius sighed. We spent the next hour discovering that I had not invented anything miraculous. Side pressure along a wet boundary worked sometimes. Not always. Thicker black veins released more cleanly. Fine branching contamination remained difficult. The material varied. Of course it varied. Real materials hated elegant theories. Still. By midday we had three piles.</p><p>Clean enough green. Questionable green. Black-heavy waste. Nera weighed them. Then weighed the original sample.</p><p>"Thirty-eight percent clean on first pass."</p><p>Corven frowned.</p><p>"That's bad?"</p><p>"That's honest," Nera said.</p><p>"Second pass on questionable?"</p><p>"Maybe another twenty."</p><p>"Labor?"</p><p>"Too much by hand." </p><p>I looked at the spoon. Shape. Pressure. Boundary. Repeatability. A tool could do this. Not Arlo. I looked away. </p><p>Antonius caught it.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Nothing."</p><p>"Greg."</p><p>"A clamp."</p><p>Nera looked over.</p><p>"Explain."</p><p>"Not a machine. A hand tool. Two shaped jaws. Hold the wet piece. Apply sideways pressure along the growth boundary. More controlled than hammering. Faster than a spoon."</p><p>Corven said, "Can you make one?"</p><p>"No." </p><p>Antonius smiled. </p><p>I pointed at him.</p><p>"Do not."</p><p>"You know someone."</p><p>"I know several people."</p><p>"Arlo."</p><p>"He's busy."</p><p>That surprised Antonius.</p><p>Good.</p><p>I meant it. Arlo had a regulator. A reference set. A problem already narrowed. I was not going to arrive with poisonous green rocks and a new industry because my brain had discovered another door. Not today.</p><p>"Any competent toolmaker," I said. "It's a clamp."</p><p>Nera nodded slowly.</p><p>"Wood first."</p><p>"Exactly."</p><p>"Different jaw shapes."</p><p>"Exactly."</p><p>"Replaceable inserts." </p><p>I stopped. That was better.</p><p>"Yes," Nera said. She smiled.</p><p>I liked her less. Antonius said, "Cost?" Nera looked at Corven.</p><p>"To develop?"</p><p>"To know whether this can become worth doing," Antonius said.</p><p>Nera thought.</p><p>"Another day."</p><p>"Money."</p><p>"One gold."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Then use spoons," I said.</p><p>I held mine up.</p><p>"Scalable."</p><p>No one laughed. Philistines. Antonius negotiated her to seven silver plus first right to buy a small batch at a fixed price. Corven agreed to provide material. Nera agreed to document handling. I agreed to nothing. That was the victory. I stood in the yard with green residue on my gloves, a page full of notes, and absolutely no ownership in a new vairglass processing venture.</p><p>It felt unnatural. Antonius took the notes.</p><p>"Good."</p><p>"I wrote them."</p><p>"I know."</p><p>"Those are mine."</p><p>"You were working for me."</p><p>"Copies." </p><p>He considered.</p><p>"Fine."</p><p>Growth. I smiled. He frowned.</p><p>"Don't."</p><p>We walked back toward his warehouse. For three streets, I managed not to mention the dungeon. Then I failed.</p><p>"How dangerous was it?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Corven went in and came out."</p><p>"No."</p><p>"That's evidence."</p><p>"It's evidence that Corven came out."</p><p>"Party size?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Depth?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Monster profile?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Mana density?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Traps?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Architecture?"</p><p>"No."</p><p>"How far from Carrow?"</p><p>"No," Antonius said.</p><p>I shoved my hands into my pockets.</p><p>"This is unreasonable."</p><p>"You are not going."</p><p>"I know."</p><p>"You say that like you're planning around the sentence."</p><p>"I'm gathering information."</p><p>"For what?"</p><p>Good question. I almost answered automatically. Future. Preparation. Opportunity. Training. But those were category words. Not reasons. What would I do with the information today? Nothing. What could I do with it? Obsess. Design. Spend money. Recruit people. Distract Arlo. Annoy Hessa. Probably attempt to accelerate my body into a dungeon before it was ready.</p><p>I hated the clarity.</p><p>"Nothing," I said. </p><p>Antonius looked at me.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"Nothing."</p><p>"That's new."</p><p>"Fuck you."</p><p>We kept walking. At the warehouse, Corven's sacks were being transferred into rigid bins under Nera's handling instructions. Slowly. No panic. No dust. A problem had become a process. I liked that. Antonius stopped beside the first sealed bin.</p><figure class="chapter-art scene-illustration"><img alt="The Sealed Bin" decoding="async" loading="lazy" onerror="this.closest('figure').remove()" src="../visual/chapter_art/012/v28_c12_s04_the-sealed-bin.png"/></figure><p>"How much do you think it's worth?"</p><p>"The vairglass?"</p><p>"All of it."</p><p>I considered. Old Greg would have multiplied clean yield by retail price and produced a number impressive enough to make everyone stupid. Current Greg had been learning. Against his will.</p><p>"Unknown." </p><p>Antonius nodded. I hated that too.</p><p>"Raw material has a floor if Nera buys it. Better value if separation works. But we don't know yield across the whole lot, labor, buyer depth, transport, spoilage, whether the chamber is repeatable, or whether Corven can safely recover more."</p><p>"Good."</p><p>"Stop sounding pleased."</p><p>"Why?"</p><p>"Because I miss when you thought I was an idiot."</p><p>"I still think you're an idiot."</p><p>"Professionally."</p><p>"Professionally, you're occasionally useful."</p><p>There it was. Not praise.</p><p>Better.</p><p>I looked at the sealed bin. Green glass. Black veins. Yesterday it had been a mysterious dungeon treasure. Today it was a hazardous raw material with a possible market and an annoying processing constraint. Much less magical. Much more real. I thought of the healer's tent, the covered bucket, the woman whose face I still could not remember.</p><p>Forty years from now, I would know this material well enough to forget where I learned it. Knowledge in my first life had accumulated until it felt like mine, even though almost none of it had begun with me. Someone had taught me. Someone had tested. Someone had gotten sick. Someone had written the handling rule.</p><p>I had returned with the result and mistaken it for possession. Uncomfortable. Useful. I said, "I want to go." </p><p>Antonius did not ask where.</p><p>"No."</p><p>"Eventually."</p><p>"Maybe."</p><p>That was different. I looked at him. He looked back.</p><p>"What?"</p><p>"You said maybe."</p><p>"I regret it."</p><p>"Too late."</p><p>"Greg."</p><p>"Eventually."</p><p>"When you can go into a warehouse without trying to cast magic at poison."</p><p>"I did not cast magic at poison."</p><p>"Because I stopped you."</p><p>"Still counts."</p><p>"No."</p><p>I grinned. He went inside. I stayed beside the bin for another moment. Dungeon. Not yet. That hurt less than it had yesterday. Not because I wanted it less. Because for once, not yet had edges. Mana. Body. Barrier. Judgment. A party I did not have. Skills I remembered but could not yet perform. There were things between me and the dungeon.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Things between meant a path. I touched the spoon in my pocket. Then immediately removed my hand because I had just spent a morning learning not to touch objects after handling deadroot. Progress. I went to wash my hands.</p></article><nav class="chapter-nav chapter-nav-top" aria-label="Chapter navigation"><a rel="prev" href="011.html">← Chapter 8</a><a href="../index.html#books">Chapters</a><a rel="next" href="013.html">Chapter 10 →</a></nav></main></body></html>
- `chapters/127.html:3`: <html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"/><meta content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1" name="viewport"/><title>Chapter 102: The Repeater — Peg-Leg Greg</title><link href="../assets/reader.css" rel="stylesheet"/></head><body><header class="site-head"><a href="../index.html">PEG-LEG GREG</a><nav aria-label="Reader navigation" class="site-nav"><a href="../art.html">ART</a></nav></header><main class="chapter-shell"><header class="chapter-title"><div class="number">CHAPTER 102</div><h1>THE REPEATER</h1></header><article class="prose"><p>Hessa had the same two threads. I checked. Same frame. Same glazed tile. Same copper. Same dark thread. Same spacing. Probably. I looked closer.</p><p>Hessa said:</p><p>“Sit down.”</p><p>“I am checking whether you changed it.”</p><p>“I changed one thing.”</p><p>I stopped.</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“Sit.”</p><p>I sat. She checked me first. Hands. Right calf. Residual limb. Phantom. Thumb. Fingers. Wrist. Grip. No surprises. The phantom foot was mildly cold despite not existing. Ordinary. Hessa pressed along my right forearm.</p><p>“Yesterday?”</p><p>“No magic.”</p><p>“Thread?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“String?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Cord?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>“You are expanding the prohibition.”</p><p>“You went to Guild.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Courier?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Did you tie anything to anything?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>“That question is absurd.”</p><p>“You are creative when annoyed.”</p><p>“I repaired a horse with wood.”</p><p>“Not yesterday.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>She went to the apparatus.</p><p>“What changed?”</p><p>She pointed at the two threads. Small paper sleeves covered the upper inch of each. One white. One gray.</p><p>“That.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“So I stop thinking of them as near and far while I record.”</p><p>I stared.</p><p>“You know which is which.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That does not work.”</p><p>“It helps.”</p><p>“How?”</p><p>“It makes me write white and gray instead of the conclusion I expect.”</p><p>“That is not blinding.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Barely even pretending.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then why?”</p><p>“Because perfect is not available.”</p><p>She moved the frame. Not far. Half an inch. Then put it back against two charcoal marks on the table. I noticed those too.</p><p>“You marked the feet.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“To preserve position.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That is a second change.”</p><p>“The marks were there last time.”</p><p>I looked. They were faint. I had missed them. Annoying. Hessa adjusted the tile.</p><p>“Question today is replication.”</p><p>I liked the word. She saw that.</p><p>“Do not.”</p><p>“I did nothing.”</p><p>“You liked it.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Stop.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She ignored me.</p><p>“Same bounded sequence. Same target region. Same approximate geometry. Same near comparison and farther comparison. One attempt.”</p><p>“Same charcoal mark?”</p><p>“Re-drawn from my notes.”</p><p>“So not exactly.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Same thread?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Same cup?”</p><p>“What cup?”</p><p>“Nothing.”</p><p>She looked at me. I looked back. Horse stayed out of this room. Good.</p><p>“What counts as replication?” I asked.</p><p>“Nothing by itself.”</p><p>“That is not an answer.”</p><p>“It is the answer you need.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“If the closer thread again shows a movement toward your arm during REACH while the farther thread does not at the same time, that would be another observation of the same general pattern.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“If it does not, that is also information.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“If both move together, information.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“If the farther moves and the closer does not, information.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“If neither moves, information.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“So everything is information.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>“That is convenient.”</p><p>“It is only convenient if you do not care what the information says.”</p><figure class="chapter-art scene-illustration"><img src="../visual/chapter_art/127/Ch127_Sleeved-Threads-and-Door.jpg" alt="Hessa opens the assessment-room door and watches the differently sleeved threads move while Greg observes." loading="lazy"/></figure><p>I did. Obviously. She opened the door. Waited. Both threads moved. White more. Gray less. She wrote. Closed door. Waited. Neither. She walked past the table. Gray trembled. White did not. She wrote. Opened the window a finger width.</p><p>Both moved left. Not together. White first. Gray second. She wrote. Closed it. We waited. The room settled. Mostly. Hessa moved my chair into position. Right forearm beside the closer thread. I could tell which sleeve was closer.</p><p>White. So could Hessa. This was not blinding. Still. She had changed how she wrote. Maybe that mattered. I breathed normally. White moved slightly away from me. Gray rotated. Hessa wrote. White returned near its line.</p><p>Gray stopped left of its line.</p><p>“Baseline is worse today,” I said.</p><p>“Different.”</p><p>“More movement.”</p><p>“So far.”</p><p>“Humidity?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>“Wet yesterday.”</p><p>“Outside.”</p><p>“Could affect room.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Thread moisture.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Air.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Heat.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Static less likely if damp.”</p><p>“Less likely is not absent.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>I wanted to ask how long we were going to watch thread before doing anything. I did not. Five minutes. Maybe six. Long enough that my right shoulder became aware of the chair. Not pain.</p><p>Position. Hessa moved the chair back.</p><p>“Reset.”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“You shifted.”</p><p>“I breathed.”</p><p>“You also leaned.”</p><p>“I did not.”</p><p>“You did.”</p><p>“How much?”</p><p>“Enough that I noticed.”</p><p>“That is not measurement.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She made me stand. I did. She reset the chair against a floor mark I had not noticed. Of course there was a floor mark. I sat again.</p><p>“Do not hold yourself rigid.”</p><p>“I wasn't.”</p><p>“You are now.”</p><p>“Because you said I moved.”</p><p>“Normal posture.”</p><p>“That is impossible after instruction.”</p><p>“Greg.”</p><p>“Fine.”</p><p>I tried to forget my spine. Failed. Eventually succeeded enough. Hessa waited another two minutes.</p><p>“Draw.”</p><p>Minimal. Right forearm. Copper answered. Small. Stable. No thumb. No finger. No wrist. No left response.</p><p>“Shape.”</p><p>Same region. Or as close to same as memory and charcoal allowed. Localized alteration. Near edge slightly more distinct. Upper edge faint. Center changed. I reported each.</p><p>“Hold.”</p><p>Held. White thread moved. Small. Away from my arm. I saw it. Hessa had not told me to look away yet. My chest sank. Interesting. Disappointing. Useful. Probably. Gray moved a moment later. Toward the window.</p><p>Hessa wrote.</p><p>“That was during shape,” she said.</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Keep it there.”</p><p>“REACH.”</p><p>I looked at her hand. Two fingers above copper. Same as last time. Smallest extension. Toward the closer thread. No force. No push. Maintain draw. The near edge sharpened. Asymmetry toward target. Familiar now.</p><p>Not comfortable. Familiar.</p><p>“Near edge sharper.”</p><p>“Continue same instruction.”</p><p>I did. Nothing else internally. No broadening. No motor. No urge. No thumb. Hessa watched past me. I watched her fingers. One breath. Two. Three.</p><p>“Hold.”</p><p>Held.</p><p>“RETURN.”</p><p>I returned. Altered region softened. Center diminished. Upper edge faded. Underlying draw stayed.</p><p>“Hold.”</p><p>Held.</p><p>“Release.”</p><p>Released. Hessa was at my wrist immediately. Open. Close. Thumb. Wrist. Grip. Again. Fine. She checked the forearm. Then the left. Then made me wait. I looked at the threads. White rested almost on its charcoal line.</p><p>Gray sat a little right.</p><p>“What happened?”</p><p>Hessa wrote first. That was cruel.</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“White moved during shape.”</p><p>“I saw.”</p><p>“Away from your arm.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Gray moved shortly after.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“During REACH?”</p><p>I waited. She finished the line.</p><p>“Neither moved enough for me to mark.”</p><p>I stared.</p><p>“Neither.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>“Nothing.”</p><p>“Nothing I recorded.”</p><p>“During the entire REACH?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“White didn't move toward me.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Gray?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“So it did not replicate.”</p><p>“The specific differential movement from last time did not replicate today.”</p><p>There was the sentence. I disliked it. It was clean.</p><p>“Could still have been mana last time.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Could be mana today without movement.”</p><p>“That question is not useful.”</p><p>“It is possible.”</p><p>“Many things are possible.”</p><p>“Could the shape have changed the thread during the movement away?”</p><p>“You had not begun REACH.”</p><p>“I was shaping.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That is still mana.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>I looked at her. She raised one finger.</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“You cannot just exclude it.”</p><p>“I am not excluding it.”</p><p>“You are.”</p><p>“I am refusing to move the question because today's answer disappointed you.”</p><p>I stopped. That landed. I hated when she did that.</p><p>“The test was REACH.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“The movement during shape was not the target observation.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>“But it happened.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And could matter.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then record it.”</p><p>“I did.”</p><p>Fine.</p><p>“What does it mean?”</p><p>“I don't know.”</p><p>“Useful.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You use that phrase badly.”</p><p>“I use it accurately.”</p><p>She sat. I remained in the test chair.</p><p>“Last time,” she said, “closer thread moved toward your arm during REACH while farther did not at that moment.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Today, it did not.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That lowers my confidence that we are seeing a repeatable external response under this setup.”</p><p>There. Actual movement. Down. Not up. I did not like it. I also trusted it more because I did not like it. Probably dangerous thought.</p><p>“What about internal control?”</p><p>“Still good.”</p><p>“Same?”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>“That is not a number.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Better confidence?”</p><p>She looked at her notes.</p><p>“Fourteenth successful minimal supervised draw.”</p><p>I waited.</p><p>“Tenth supervised shaping attempt.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Third supervised external attempt.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You established the localized alteration at the intended shifted region.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You maintained underlying draw.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You attempted one bounded REACH without broadening, force sensation, motor recruitment, thumb symptom, wrist movement, elbowward shift, or unusual left response.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You RETURNed promptly.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“So yes. My confidence in that sequence increases again.”</p><p>I nodded. External down. Internal up. Annoying. Balanced. Probably.</p><p>“What next?”</p><p>“No magic tomorrow.”</p><p>I closed my eyes.</p><p>“One day.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then assessment?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“External?”</p><p>“Assessment.”</p><p>“You enjoy that.”</p><p>“A little.”</p><p>I opened my eyes.</p><p>“Are you going to use the same threads again?”</p><p>“I don't know.”</p><p>“You must have a plan.”</p><p>“I have several.”</p><p>“Which?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Because I want to decide after I review all three attempts, not while you are sitting here trying to make one of them win.”</p><p>“I am not trying to make it win.”</p><p>“You are arguing that movement during shape should count.”</p><p>“It should be recorded.”</p><p>“It was.”</p><p>“Then yes.”</p><p>She almost smiled.</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>I looked at the white sleeve.</p><p>“Why keep the paper labels if you know which is near?”</p><p>“Because I noticed something in my own notes.”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“I wrote ‘near moved’ more quickly than I wrote the actual direction.”</p><p>I looked at her.</p><p>“That is bad.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You are admitting error.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Are you ill?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Should I check your grip?”</p><p>“Greg.”</p><p>“Fine.”</p><p>She tapped the page.</p><p>“Near is already interpretation. White is an object.”</p><figure class="chapter-art scene-illustration"><img src="../visual/chapter_art/127/Ch127_Fast-Coverage-005-01.jpg" alt="A sketch-style story scene from Chapter 127." loading="lazy"/></figure><p>“That seems excessive.”</p><p>“Probably.”</p><p>“Then why do it?”</p><p>“Cheap.”</p><p>I had no answer. She won. Again. I pointed at the gray cloth.</p><p>“Are you changing the apparatus next time?”</p><p>“I said I don't know.”</p><p>“The comparison is imperfect.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Local heat differs.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Distance differs.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Air around my arm differs.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Thread behavior differs.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“So improve it.”</p><p>“How?”</p><p>“Put a second target at the same distance from another part of me.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Because then you are changing what you are doing internally.”</p><p>“Not necessarily.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“I could shape two regions.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Not simultaneously.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Separate trials.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Because I am not doubling your shaping to improve my thread experiment.”</p><p>That was irritatingly reasonable.</p><p>“Then use a barrier between the threads.”</p><p>“That changes airflow.”</p><p>“Shield both.”</p><p>“Changes the room.”</p><p>“Enclose the frame.”</p><p>“Heat.”</p><p>“Larger enclosure.”</p><p>“Greg.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You are trying to design the perfect apparatus.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“There isn't one.”</p><p>“There can be a better one.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then why not?”</p><p>“Because better for one confound can be worse for another, and because I also care whether the same simple setup ever gives the same result twice.”</p><p>I looked at the covered frame.</p><p>“That is why you repeated it unchanged.”</p><p>“Mostly unchanged.”</p><p>“Paper sleeves.”</p><p>“Those are for me.”</p><p>“Still changed.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You hate that.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>Good. At least the universe remained stable.</p><p>“What if the next test is different?”</p><p>“Then I will tell you the question before you do anything.”</p><p>“And if it is the same?”</p><p>“Same.”</p><p>“One attempt?”</p><p>“Probably.”</p><p>“No magic after?”</p><p>“Depends.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“Assessment.”</p><p>I hated that word almost as much as unestablished. She gathered the copper and set it beside her notes. I noticed three pages. One for each external attempt. The first page had more writing than the other two.</p><p>Of course it did. Messier question. Messier notes.</p><p>“What are you looking for when you review?”</p><p>“Patterns.”</p><p>“That is vague.”</p><p>“Symptoms first.”</p><p>“None.”</p><p>“So far.”</p><p>“Then control sequence.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then apparatus behavior before, during, after.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then whether anything I thought mattered was actually just memorable.”</p><p>I stopped.</p><p>“What?”</p><p>She tapped the first page.</p><p>“Two movements are memorable.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Memorable is not the same as diagnostic.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>The second page.</p><p>“One differential movement is memorable.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“The third page refusing to repeat it is also memorable.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>She stacked them.</p><p>“That is why I am reviewing all three.”</p><p>Not to decide which story she liked. Fine. I understood. Still wanted the thread to move. Hessa covered the frame. Gray cloth. Threads gone.</p><p>“No magic tomorrow.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No thread.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No hanging cord.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No clever substitutes.”</p><p>“I am not going to move dust.”</p><p>She stared.</p><p>“I was making a joke.”</p><p>“Do not move dust.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“Go.”</p><p>I went. Outside, I stood for a moment. The result should have disappointed me more. It did disappoint me. I wanted the thread to move. Again. Same direction. Same timing. I wanted a clean line through three observations and a conclusion at the end.</p><p>Instead:</p><p>First test ambiguous. Second test suggestive. Third test did not repeat the suggestive part. That was not failure. It was not success. It was science being an asshole. I walked. Not Guild. Not theatre.</p><p>Not Lyssa. At the first corner I nearly turned toward Hessa again. Not to argue. To ask one more question. Different problem. Same behavior. I kept going. A baker had set two trays near the open window.</p><p>One sweet. One not. I could smell the sweet one from across the street. That was enough information to make me cross. No. Stop. I bought a pear instead because I had already committed to not turning lunch into a system.</p><p>The pear seller gave me the softer of two without asking. I noticed.</p><p>“Why that one?”</p><p>“You'll eat it now.”</p><p>“How do you know?”</p><p>“You're holding it.”</p><p>“That happened after you chose it.”</p><p>She looked at me.</p><p>“Do you want the hard one?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Then go away.”</p><p>I went away. Carrow remained hostile to inquiry. I bought a pear. Sat on a low wall. A dog stared at me. I stared back. The dog looked away first. Established external effect. No.</p><p>I ate the pear. A cart went past. Not Sevren. A woman carrying flowers stopped to retie one bundle. Two boys argued about whether a roof tile had fallen today or yesterday. Nobody knew.</p><p>The dog came back. Sat near my right crutch. Brown. One white paw. Its left ear folded at the tip. It watched my pear with professional attention. I shifted the core from my right hand to my left.</p><p>Its eyes followed. That was an external effect. No. That was a dog. I did not test anything on it. Good. I put the pear core on the wall beside me instead. The dog looked at it.</p><p>Then at me. Then at it. This was already a better experiment than thread because the dog clearly wanted something. Also worse because dogs had opinions. It stood. Took one step toward the wall.</p><p>Stopped. I did nothing. The dog sat again.</p><p>“Your controls are terrible,” I told it.</p><p>Its tail moved once. Could be wind. I laughed before I could stop myself. A man passing with a sack looked at me.</p><p>“Dog won't eat pear.”</p><p>“I can see that.”</p><p>“He'll eat sausage.”</p><p>“I don't have sausage.”</p><p>“Then you've designed badly.”</p><p>He kept walking. I stared after him. Everyone in Carrow had become Hessa. Unacceptable. My forearm felt normal. Hands normal. Residual limb quiet. Phantom toes appeared briefly when I shifted. Ordinary. Tomorrow no magic.</p><p>Fine. I finished the pear. The dog watched the core. I held it out. It sniffed. Did not take it. Non-replication.</p><p>“Fuck you too.”</p><p>The dog left. I laughed. Then went home.</p></article><nav class="chapter-nav chapter-nav-top" aria-label="Chapter navigation"><a rel="prev" href="126.html">← Chapter 101</a><a href="../index.html#books">Chapters</a><a rel="next" href="128.html">Chapter 103 →</a></nav></main></body></html>
- `chapters/109.html:3`: <html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"/><meta content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1" name="viewport"/><title>Chapter 86: The Stopper — Peg-Leg Greg</title><link href="../assets/reader.css" rel="stylesheet"/></head><body><header class="site-head"><a href="../index.html">PEG-LEG GREG</a><nav aria-label="Reader navigation" class="site-nav"><a href="../art.html">ART</a><a href="../r2/">R2</a></nav></header><main class="chapter-shell"><header class="chapter-title"><div class="number">CHAPTER 86</div><h1>THE STOPPER</h1></header><article class="prose"><p>Hessa drew a line on my forearm.</p><p>Not a dot.</p><p>Progress.</p><p>“Charcoal again?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You have limited artistic range.”</p><p>“I am devastated.”</p><p>The line was short.</p><p>Maybe the width of my little finger.</p><p>It sat on the inside of my right forearm, several inches above the wrist.</p><p>I looked at it.</p><p>Then at Hessa.</p><p>“New target.”</p><p>“Not exactly.”</p><p>“What does that mean?”</p><p>“It means today I care less about reaching the mark.”</p><p>I stopped.</p><p>That was different.</p><p>My right hand had stayed quiet since the second tingling episode.</p><p>No recurrence after the successful shaping attempt.</p><p>No recurrence during cards.</p><p>No recurrence overnight.</p><p>No pain.</p><p>No weakness.</p><p>No numbness.</p><p>No cold.</p><p>Residual limb baseline.</p><p>Hands fine.</p><p>Right calf fine.</p><p>Everything boring enough that I had become suspicious of boredom again.</p><p>Hessa had examined me.</p><p>Then forearm.</p><p>Then hand.</p><p>Then drawn the line.</p><p>“What&#x27;s the question?”</p><p>“Whether you can stop.”</p><p>“I stopped last time.”</p><p>“You released.”</p><p>“At your instruction.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That is stopping.”</p><p>“Not the same thing.”</p><p>I leaned back in the bad chair.</p><p>“Explain.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>She put the straight copper strip on the table.</p><p>Folded towel.</p><p>No ceramic dish this time.</p><p>The charcoal nub remained in her hand.</p><p>She added a second small line farther up the forearm.</p><p>Two marks now.</p><p>I stared.</p><p>“That is worse.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>“Two marks imply a choice.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Which one?”</p><p>“You don&#x27;t know yet.”</p><p>“I dislike this.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>“You are enjoying this.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>She set the charcoal aside.</p><p>“Minimal draw first.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then I will tell you which line.”</p><p>“During the draw?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And I alter toward it?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“How far?”</p><p>“Until I tell you stop.”</p><p>There.</p><p>My pulse changed.</p><p>“Then?”</p><p>“You stop altering.”</p><p>“Hold the draw?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>That was the new part.</p><p>Not release.</p><p>Stop the alteration while keeping the draw stable.</p><p>I sat more upright.</p><p>Hessa noticed.</p><p>“Do not get excited.”</p><p>“That instruction has never worked.”</p><p>“One attempt.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“If you feel the familiar broad hand-and-wrist pattern, stop and release.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“If you feel pain, tingling, weakness, cold, numbness, or anything you think is wrong, stop and release.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“If your wrist begins moving.”</p><p>“Stop and release.”</p><p>“If I say stop.”</p><p>“Stop altering but keep the draw.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“For how long?”</p><p>“Until I tell you release.”</p><p>“That introduces timing.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“How long?”</p><p>“You do not.”</p><p>“Cruel.”</p><p>“Useful.”</p><p>Maybe.</p><p>No.</p><p>Not saying that word.</p><p>I looked at the two lines.</p><p>One nearer the wrist.</p><p>One farther up.</p><p>Both on intact right forearm.</p><p>No left side.</p><p>No phantom question.</p><p>Good.</p><p>“What if I cannot tell whether the alteration stopped?”</p><p>“Report that.”</p><p>“What if I overshoot?”</p><p>“Report that.”</p><p>“What counts as overshoot?”</p><p>“Greg.”</p><p>“Fine.”</p><p>I put my right forearm on the towel.</p><p>Palm up.</p><p>The lines faced me.</p><p>Hessa rotated my arm slightly so they faced more toward her.</p><p>“Do not use vision once we start.”</p><p>“You drew them where I can see them.”</p><p>“Now you know where they are.”</p><p>“Approximate.”</p><p>“Enough.”</p><p>She raised the copper.</p><p>“Ready?”</p><p>I breathed.</p><p>No rehearsal.</p><p>No trying to pre-build the sensation.</p><p>Just ready.</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Draw.”</p><p>I drew.</p><p>Mana came.</p><p>Small.</p><p>Stable.</p><p>Chest.</p><p>Shoulders.</p><p>Arms.</p><p>Right side.</p><p>Left thigh.</p><p>Knee.</p><p>Ordinary phantom foot.</p><p>Nothing unusual below.</p><p>Right hand quiet.</p><p>Forearm quiet.</p><p>“Stable?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Far line.”</p><p>I almost looked.</p><p>Did not.</p><p>Alter.</p><p>Toward the farther line.</p><p>This was not hand.</p><p>Forearm felt different.</p><p>Less precise.</p><p>Or I was less familiar with attending to it.</p><p>Mana did not move like water.</p><p>Again.</p><p>Stop using water.</p><p>Something shifted.</p><p>A narrow band?</p><p>No.</p><p>A patch.</p><p>Longer than last time.</p><p>Along the inside of the forearm.</p><p>Moving upward.</p><p>Not physically.</p><p>Magically.</p><p>Probably.</p><p>I wanted to know where it was.</p><p>No visual check.</p><figure class="chapter-art sketch-beat"><img src="../visual/chapter_art/109/Ch109_Stop-Forearm-Test.png" alt="Hessa calls a stop as Greg holds still during the controlled forearm test." loading="lazy"/></figure><p>Hessa said, “Stop.”</p><p>I stopped.</p><p>Or tried.</p><p>The alteration continued for a fraction.</p><p>Maybe.</p><p>Then held.</p><p>My entire attention narrowed.</p><p>Draw still present.</p><p>Alteration no longer moving.</p><p>I thought.</p><p>Then the patch widened.</p><p>Fuck.</p><p>Not upward.</p><p>Sideways.</p><p>Broader across the forearm.</p><p>I had stopped direction, not change.</p><p>“It&#x27;s spreading,” I said.</p><p>“Release.”</p><p>I released.</p><p>Everything went.</p><p>My forearm remained on the towel.</p><p>Hessa lowered the copper.</p><p>“Report.”</p><p>“I failed.”</p><p>“Report.”</p><p>“Draw stable.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You called far line.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“I made a localized change moving toward it.”</p><p>“Continue.”</p><p>“When you said stop, I stopped the movement toward the line.”</p><p>“Think.”</p><p>“I attempted to.”</p><p>“Better.”</p><p>“I think it stopped moving upward.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then the altered area widened sideways.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“I did not intend that.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“No wrist movement.”</p><p>“I saw none.”</p><p>“No hand spread.”</p><p>“I saw none.”</p><p>“No Barrier-like setup.”</p><p>“I saw none.”</p><p>“Pain none. Tingling none. Numbness none. Cold none. Weakness none.”</p><p>“Below knee?”</p><p>“Ordinary phantom only.”</p><p>“Did you feel the widening before you reported it?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“How long?”</p><p>“Very short.”</p><p>“That is not a duration.”</p><p>“You trained me.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>I looked at the forearm.</p><p>No visible change.</p><p>Only charcoal.</p><p>“Copper?”</p><p>“Responded during the alteration.”</p><p>“During the widening?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>That mattered.</p><p>“Then it was real.”</p><p>“It was observable.”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Fuck you.”</p><p>“Consistent language.”</p><p>I laughed.</p><p>She wrote.</p><p>I waited.</p><p>This time I did not ask immediately.</p><p>Personal record.</p><p>Five breaths.</p><p>Maybe six.</p><p>Not timing.</p><p>She finished.</p><p>“What did you see?”</p><p>“A more elongated alteration than the prior hand target.”</p><p>“Toward far line?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Did it reach?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“How far?”</p><p>“I am not giving you inches.”</p><p>“Coward.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then after stop?”</p><p>“The forward progression reduced.”</p><p>“Reduced?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Not stopped?”</p><p>“Not cleanly enough for me to call it stopped.”</p><p>That hurt.</p><p>Fine.</p><p>“And widened.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“How much?”</p><p>“Enough to distinguish.”</p><p>“So I did not stop.”</p><p>“You changed what it was doing.”</p><p>I looked up.</p><p>There.</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“The alteration did not continue in exactly the same way after the stop instruction.”</p><p>“But it kept changing.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“So I partially controlled it.”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>I groaned.</p><p>“Use your own word.”</p><p>“I am.”</p><p>“What is the question now?”</p><p>“Whether you can stop deliberate shaping without releasing the draw.”</p><p>“And answer?”</p><p>“Not cleanly from this attempt.”</p><p>“Because it widened.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“But it changed direction.”</p><p>“Perhaps.”</p><p>“Perhaps?”</p><p>“Your report says forward movement stopped. My observation says the pattern changed. That does not prove you deliberately redirected it. It may have broadened because control degraded.”</p><p>That was worse.</p><p>Also better.</p><p>I hated both.</p><p>“So the failure is specific.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“I can initiate a small unfamiliar alteration.”</p><p>“We have some evidence for that.”</p><p>“I can respond to a stop instruction enough to change the pattern.”</p><p>“We have one observation consistent with that.”</p><p>“But I cannot yet hold it unchanged.”</p><p>“We do not know if you can. You did not today.”</p><p>There.</p><p>Clean.</p><p>I nodded.</p><p>No breakthrough.</p><p>No collapse.</p><p>A narrow failure.</p><p>Useful.</p><p>“What would happen if you told me stop earlier?”</p><p>“I am not testing that today.”</p><p>“Of course.”</p><p>“One attempt.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Do you understand why?”</p><p>“Because repetition trains.”</p><p>“And?”</p><p>“Because widening was unintended.”</p><p>“And?”</p><p>“Because you want delayed observation.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And because you hate me.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Unproven.”</p><p>She examined my forearm.</p><p>Temperature.</p><p>Skin.</p><p>Hand.</p><p>Grip.</p><p>Wrist.</p><p>Normal.</p><p>Then waited.</p><p>I waited too.</p><p>This part had become familiar in the worst possible way.</p><p>The bad chair.</p><p>The wall crack.</p><p>Nerin moving in the outer room.</p><p>Someone talking quietly.</p><p>Street noise.</p><p>No thumb tingling.</p><p>No forearm tingling.</p><p>No pain.</p><p>Nothing.</p><p>I looked at the two charcoal lines.</p><p>“Can I wash them off?”</p><p>“Not yet.”</p><p>“Again?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“What if charcoal is causing the magical effect?”</p><p>Hessa stared.</p><p>“I wanted to see if you had limits.”</p><p>“There they are.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>I leaned back.</p><p>“What does this do to casting prognosis?”</p><p>“Almost nothing.”</p><p>“Almost?”</p><p>“It gives me another piece of evidence that you can deliberately initiate alteration.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And another piece that control after initiation is not yet clean.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That is unsurprising.”</p><p>“Rude.”</p><p>“It is early.”</p><p>There.</p><p>Early.</p><p>Not impossible.</p><p>Not recovered.</p><p>Early.</p><p>I liked that word too much.</p><p>“What about spells that don&#x27;t require holding?”</p><p>“Later.”</p><p>“What about spells where release is the end?”</p><p>“Later.”</p><p>“What about Barrier?”</p><p>“Later.”</p><p>“Could releasing have been the correct stop?”</p><p>“For a spell, perhaps. Not for today&#x27;s question.”</p><p>“Because you wanted separation between altering and drawing.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And the ability to stop one without ending the other.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Why?”</p><p>She paused.</p><p>I waited.</p><p>Actually waited.</p><p>Then she answered.</p><p>“Because if every shaping change can only end by dropping the entire draw, you have less control than I want before testing anything with an external effect.”</p><p>That shut me up.</p><p>External effect.</p><p>Not next.</p><p>Not promised.</p><p>But category.</p><p>There.</p><p>I did not smile.</p><p>Probably.</p><p>Hessa saw anyway.</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“I said nothing.”</p><p>“You heard future.”</p><p>“I heard criteria.”</p><p>“You heard future.”</p><p>“Both can be true.”</p><p>She sighed.</p><p>“What would external mean?”</p><p>“Not today.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>“Then do not make me define a test I am not planning.”</p><p>“Fine.”</p><p>We waited.</p><p>No symptoms.</p><p>Eventually Hessa said, “Move fingers.”</p><p>Normal.</p><p>“Wrist.”</p><p>Normal.</p><p>“Grip.”</p><p>Normal.</p><p>“Stand.”</p><p>Crutches.</p><p>Right hand grip.</p><p>Up.</p><p>No tingling.</p><p>Walk to door.</p><p>Back.</p><p>No symptoms.</p><figure class="chapter-art scene-illustration"><img src="../visual/chapter_art/109/Ch109_Fast-Coverage-003-C18.jpg" alt="A sketch-style story scene from Chapter 109." loading="lazy"/></figure><p>She let me wash the charcoal off.</p><p>Two gray streaks.</p><p>Gone.</p><p>“Tomorrow?” I asked.</p><p>“No magic.”</p><p>I closed my eyes.</p><p>“You have only one tool.”</p><p>“It works.”</p><p>“Day after?”</p><p>“Come back.”</p><p>“Assessment.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Stop test again?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>“Different target?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>“Draw only?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>“You have ruined that word.”</p><p>“You keep coming back.”</p><p>Fair.</p><p>I stood.</p><p>At the door:</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“If I had held the change after stop, would that have counted as success?”</p><p>She considered.</p><p>“For today&#x27;s instruction, yes.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>“You did not.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>I smiled.</p><p>That confused her slightly.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Failure with a shape.</p><p>Better than fog.</p><p>I left.</p><p>Outside, I had no dramatic desire to tell everyone.</p><p>That surprised me.</p><p>I still wanted to tell Lyssa.</p><p>And Jorren.</p><p>Maybe Alden.</p><p>But not immediately.</p><p>The result was less shiny.</p><p>More technical.</p><p>I liked it anyway.</p><p>I went to the Guild.</p><p>Merrin looked up.</p><p>“Work?”</p><p>I thought.</p><p>Maybe.</p><p>No.</p><p>I wanted something else.</p><p>“What is everyone doing?”</p><p>“That is not a work request.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>He pointed toward the yard.</p><p>“Alden and Lio are arguing about distance.”</p><p>Good.</p><p>I went.</p><p>Not training.</p><p>Watching.</p><p>The yard was active.</p><p>Pessa had three people moving between marked lines.</p><p>Alden stood near the wall with Lio, both looking at an arrow stuck in a target.</p><p>Alden saw me.</p><p>“Settle this.”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“You don&#x27;t know the question.”</p><p>“Preventive.”</p><p>He looked offended.</p><p>Lio laughed.</p><p>“What is it?”</p><p>Alden pointed.</p><p>“That&#x27;s twelve paces.”</p><p>Lio said, “Eleven.”</p><p>I looked.</p><p>“Whose paces?”</p><p>Silence.</p><p>Good.</p><p>I had them.</p><p>Alden said, “Normal.”</p><p>“No such thing.”</p><p>“Fuck.”</p><p>Lio walked it.</p><p>Eleven of his.</p><p>Alden walked it.</p><p>Twelve of his.</p><p>They both stared.</p><p>I sat on a barrel.</p><p>“Congratulations.”</p><p>“That is stupid,” Alden said.</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“We need a measure.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>Lio looked at me.</p><p>“You have one?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Then you&#x27;re useless.”</p><p>“Correct.”</p><p>This felt excellent.</p><p>Pessa glanced over.</p><p>Saw me.</p><p>“Training?”</p><p>I checked.</p><p>Did I want to?</p><p>Body baseline.</p><p>Hand fine.</p><p>Magic test done.</p><p>Hessa had not forbidden movement.</p><p>But I had already spent attention today.</p><p>The stop test had taken more out of me mentally than physically.</p><p>I wanted to sit.</p><p>“No.”</p><p>Pessa nodded.</p><p>Nothing else.</p><p>Alden said, “Coward.”</p><p>Octavia had spread too.</p><p>“Apparently.”</p><p>I watched them argue about how to standardize distance without a measuring cord.</p><p>They eventually used the length of a practice spear laid repeatedly on the ground.</p><p>Not precise.</p><p>Better.</p><p>Lio&#x27;s “eleven” and Alden&#x27;s “twelve” became something like six-and-a-bit spear lengths.</p><p>They were both dissatisfied.</p><p>Good.</p><p>The target did not care.</p><p>Alden shot.</p><p>Missed left.</p><p>Lio shot.</p><p>Hit outer ring.</p><p>Alden blamed the distance change.</p><p>Pessa said, “You were standing in the same place.”</p><p>Jorren appeared from nowhere with an apple.</p><p>Of course.</p><p>“Magic?”</p><p>he asked.</p><p>“Failed.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>Alden lowered the bow.</p><p>“What?”</p><p>I had made a mistake.</p><p>Now there was an audience.</p><p>“Not failed magic. Failed instruction.”</p><p>“What instruction?”</p><p>“Stop.”</p><p>Jorren bit apple.</p><p>“You failed stopping?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“That sounds like you.”</p><p>“Fuck you.”</p><p>Alden handed bow back to Lio.</p><p>“Explain.”</p><p>I did the short version.</p><p>New forearm target.</p><p>Shape toward.</p><p>Hessa says stop.</p><p>Hold draw.</p><p>Alteration stops going forward but widens.</p><p>Release.</p><p>No symptoms.</p><p>No spell.</p><p>Alden frowned.</p><p>“So you shaped again.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“And failed.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Good.”</p><p>Everyone had one word.</p><p>I hated all of them.</p><p>Lio said, “Could you feel it widen?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Did it hurt?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Could you move it back?”</p><p>“Not tested.”</p><p>“Why not?”</p><p>“Hessa.”</p><p>He nodded immediately.</p><p>Professional reputation.</p><p>Useful.</p><p>Pessa had listened without appearing to.</p><p>She said, “Hand fine?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then I don&#x27;t care.”</p><p>Perfect.</p><p>Jorren handed me apple.</p><p>I took it.</p><p>“Knife?”</p><p>I asked.</p><p>He showed the dark handle at his belt.</p><p>“Always.”</p><p>“You are becoming a person who carries a food knife.”</p><p>“I carry food.”</p><p>“That is not true.”</p><p>“I intend to.”</p><p>Alden said, “Can we go back to distance?”</p><p>“No,” Jorren said.</p><p>“It was better.”</p><p>I laughed.</p><p>Then watched.</p><p>No theory.</p><p>No notebook.</p><p>Just arrows.</p><p>Alden adjusted.</p><p>Lio corrected something in his shoulder.</p><p>Pessa corrected both.</p><p>I ate apple.</p><p>At one point, my phantom left foot felt planted.</p><p>Ordinary.</p><p>I noticed.</p><p>Did nothing.</p><p>Later it was gone.</p><p>No connection.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Lyssa found me near evening.</p><p>Not because I had summoned her.</p><p>She came through the Guild yard looking for someone else first.</p><p>A woman from the freight side waved to her.</p><p>Lyssa crossed over, spoke briefly, handed her a small wrapped bundle, accepted coins, then finally looked around and saw me.</p><p>Independent business.</p><p>Good.</p><p>She came over.</p><p>“You&#x27;re sitting.”</p><p>“Apparently suspicious.”</p><p>“To everyone.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>She looked at the practice target.</p><p>“Training?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Magic?”</p><p>“Earlier.”</p><p>Her eyes changed.</p><p>“How?”</p><p>“I shaped and failed to stop.”</p><p>“That sounds complicated.”</p><p>“It was.”</p><p>“Did it hurt?”</p><p>“No.”</p><p>“Are you allowed?”</p><p>“One attempt. Supervised.”</p><p>“Hessa?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Did she look angry?”</p><p>“Normal face.”</p><p>Lyssa smiled.</p><p>“Then good.”</p><p>There it was.</p><p>Again.</p><p>I told her the short version.</p><p>She listened.</p><p>Not pretending to understand channel mechanics.</p><p>“What happens next?”</p><p>“No magic tomorrow.”</p><p>“You hate that.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“Then?”</p><p>“Assessment.”</p><p>“More stopping?”</p><p>“Maybe.”</p><p>She laughed before I could react.</p><p>Cruel.</p><p>“I hate that word.”</p><p>“I know.”</p><p>We walked out together.</p><p>Not a date.</p><p>Not declared.</p><p>She had finished work.</p><p>I was done watching arrows.</p><p>We were both hungry.</p><p>That was enough.</p><p>At the first food stall, she chose something with too much sauce.</p><p>I chose the same.</p><p>Bad strategy.</p><p>Good food.</p><p>We ate standing for her and sitting for me on a low wall.</p><p>Lyssa got sauce on one finger and wiped it on the paper wrapping.</p><p>“You&#x27;re staring.”</p><p>“At the food.”</p><p>“You&#x27;re terrible at lying.”</p><p>“I had a whole card chapter about this.”</p><p>“What?”</p><p>“Nothing.”</p><p>She took another bite.</p><p>I looked at her, then at the street.</p><p>People were closing shutters one at a time. A cart rolled past with one wheel making a soft repeated click. Someone farther down the road was arguing about whether a basket belonged inside or outside a doorway.</p><p>Carrow did not care that I had shaped mana.</p><p>Good.</p><p>Lyssa finished first.</p><p>“You want mine?”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>“You answered before I finished.”</p><p>“You were offering food.”</p><p>“I could have been asking whether you wanted the paper.”</p><p>“I would still have said yes eventually.”</p><p>She handed me the last two bites.</p><p>My hand stayed normal.</p><p>My residual limb stayed normal.</p><p>No spell had happened.</p><p>I had shaped mana and failed to stop it cleanly.</p><p>That was progress.</p><p>Not because failure was secretly success.</p><p>Because it was finally specific enough to be wrong.</p><p>I liked that.</p></article><nav class="chapter-nav chapter-nav-top" aria-label="Chapter navigation"><a rel="prev" href="107.html">← Chapter 85</a><a href="../index.html#books">Chapters</a><a rel="next" href="110.html">Chapter 87 →</a></nav></main></body></html>
